stem: A company is designing an application that processes sensitive financial transactions and must maintain a complete, tamper-proof audit log of all transactions. The log must be cryptographically verifiable, append-only, and retained for 10 years. Auditors must be able to verify that no records have been modified or deleted. Which storage solution provides cryptographic verification of data integrity?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 with Object Lock in compliance mode and versioning enabled, write transaction records as immutable objects, and use S3 checksums for integrity verification.
Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with logical replication to a read-only replica, implement trigger-based audit tables that record all changes, and use pgcrypto for hash verification.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with point-in-time recovery enabled, write all transactions with a condition expression preventing overwrites, and enable DynamoDB Streams for change tracking.
Use Amazon QLDB (Quantum Ledger Database) to store transaction records in an immutable journal with cryptographic hash chaining that provides verifiable transaction history with proofs.

explanation: QLDB provides a cryptographically verifiable, immutable journal using hash chaining. Each transaction is cryptographically linked to previous transactions, enabling auditors to prove no records were modified. DynamoDB (B) supports point-in-time recovery but doesn't provide cryptographic verification of history. S3 Object Lock (C) prevents deletion but doesn't provide chain verification between records. Aurora audit triggers (D) can be modified by database administrators and lack built-in cryptographic proofs.

stem: A company is migrating a large-scale Kubernetes deployment from on-premises to AWS. The deployment consists of 200 microservices, custom Helm charts, Istio service mesh, and Prometheus monitoring. The company wants to maintain full Kubernetes API compatibility and existing tooling. Which migration approach minimizes changes to the existing Kubernetes configuration?

options.text: Deploy Amazon EKS with managed node groups, migrate Helm charts directly, install Istio on EKS using the existing configuration, and deploy Prometheus using the Prometheus Operator.
Deploy Amazon ECS with Fargate, convert Helm charts to ECS task definitions and service definitions, replace Istio with App Mesh, and switch monitoring to CloudWatch Container Insights.
Deploy Amazon EKS Anywhere on AWS Outposts hardware to maintain identical on-premises Kubernetes experience, migrate all configurations directly without any modifications needed.
Deploy AWS App Runner for all microservices, convert Docker images to App Runner services, replace Istio service mesh with API Gateway, and use X-Ray for distributed tracing.

explanation: EKS provides full Kubernetes API compatibility, allowing direct migration of Helm charts. Istio runs on EKS natively. Prometheus Operator works unchanged. Managed node groups reduce operational overhead. ECS (B) requires converting all Kubernetes configurations to ECS format and replacing the service mesh. EKS Anywhere on Outposts (C) is for on-premises, not AWS cloud migration. App Runner (D) doesn't support Kubernetes configurations or service mesh.

stem: A company is implementing a cloud center of excellence (CCoE) for its AWS environment. The CCoE must provide standardized account provisioning, enforce security guardrails across all accounts, enable cost visibility per team, and provide a self-service portal for developers. Which TWO AWS services form the foundation of this CCoE implementation?

options.text: Amazon WorkSpaces for providing developers with standardized cloud development environments, enabling consistent tooling and secure access to AWS resources from managed desktops.
AWS Service Catalog for self-service provisioning of pre-approved infrastructure templates with launch constraints, tag options for cost attribution, and portfolio management.
AWS Trusted Advisor for automated security recommendations across all accounts, cost optimization suggestions per team, and service limit monitoring for proactive governance.
AWS Control Tower for standardized account provisioning with guardrails, account factory for self-service, and integration with AWS Organizations for centralized governance.

explanation: Control Tower provides standardized account provisioning, guardrails, and organizational governance—the foundation of a CCoE. Service Catalog provides self-service infrastructure with cost attribution via tags and governed templates. Trusted Advisor (C) provides recommendations but not provisioning, guardrails, or self-service. WorkSpaces (D) is for virtual desktops, not CCoE governance capabilities.

stem: A media streaming company needs to transcode uploaded videos into adaptive bitrate streaming formats (HLS and DASH). Each video must be transcoded into 6 quality levels. The company processes 1,000 videos per day, each averaging 2 GB in size. The solution must be cost-effective and scale automatically with upload volume. Which architecture should the architect recommend?

options.text: Deploy FFmpeg on EC2 GPU instances in an Auto Scaling group, process uploads from SQS, output transcoded files to S3, and use CloudFront for adaptive bitrate streaming delivery.
Use Amazon Elastic Transcoder to convert videos into multiple formats, trigger pipelines via S3 events, store outputs in S3 with lifecycle policies, and serve via CloudFront.
Use AWS Elemental MediaLive for real-time transcoding of uploaded videos into HLS streams, configure MediaPackage for DASH packaging, and deliver through CloudFront with signed URLs.
Use AWS Elemental MediaConvert for transcoding into HLS and DASH formats with multiple quality levels, trigger jobs via S3 events and Lambda, and deliver content through CloudFront.

explanation: MediaConvert is a file-based transcoding service that supports HLS and DASH output with multiple quality levels. It scales automatically, charges per minute of output, and requires no infrastructure management. FFmpeg on GPU instances (B) requires managing infrastructure and scaling. MediaLive (C) is for live streaming, not file-based transcoding of uploaded videos. Elastic Transcoder (D) is a legacy service with fewer features and less codec support than MediaConvert.

stem: A company operates a global application with users in 10 countries. The application runs in us-east-1 only. Users in Asia and Europe experience 300-500ms API latency due to distance. The company cannot deploy a full multi-Region architecture due to database consistency requirements, but needs to reduce latency for all users to under 200ms. Which approach reduces latency without multi-Region deployment?

options.text: Deploy AWS Global Accelerator to route user traffic over the AWS global network backbone instead of the public internet, reducing latency through optimized network routing.
Configure Route 53 geolocation routing to direct users to the closest AWS edge location, deploy API Gateway edge-optimized endpoints, and use regional DynamoDB for caching.
Add CloudFront in front of the API with aggressive caching policies for GET requests, use Lambda@Edge for personalizing cached responses, and serve static assets from edge locations.
Increase EC2 instance sizes in us-east-1 to process requests faster, optimize database queries to reduce processing time, and enable TCP keep-alive for persistent connections.

explanation: Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network backbone which provides more consistent and lower latency than the public internet. It can reduce latency by 30-60% for distant users by entering the AWS network at the nearest edge location. CloudFront caching (B) helps for cacheable content but API responses are often dynamic and uncacheable. Faster processing (C) doesn't address network transit latency. Route 53 geolocation (D) still routes to us-east-1 since there's only one Region, and edge-optimized API Gateway doesn't help for Lambda/EC2 backends.

stem: A company is migrating a stateful web application that relies on server-side sessions and file uploads stored on the local filesystem. The application is deployed on 4 servers behind a hardware load balancer with session persistence. The migration target is an elastic AWS architecture. Which set of changes makes the application cloud-ready before migration?

options.text: Move sessions to DynamoDB with TTL for expiration, store file uploads locally with rsync for synchronization between instances, deploy behind ALB with weighted target groups.
Move sessions to ElastiCache for Redis, move file uploads to S3 with pre-signed URLs for direct browser upload, deploy behind ALB, and add Auto Scaling based on CPU metrics.
Implement client-side sessions using encrypted cookies, store file uploads in EBS volumes with Multi-Attach, deploy on fixed EC2 instances, and use ALB without sticky sessions.
Keep server-side sessions with ALB sticky sessions, move file uploads to an EFS mount shared across instances, deploy in an Auto Scaling group, and use NLB for persistence.

explanation: ElastiCache externalizes sessions for stateless instances. S3 provides scalable file storage with pre-signed URLs for direct upload. ALB distributes traffic without sticky sessions. Auto Scaling enables elasticity. These changes make the application cloud-native. ALB sticky sessions with EFS (B) maintain session coupling and EFS adds complexity. Client-side sessions (C) have size limits and EBS Multi-Attach requires cluster-aware filesystems. DynamoDB sessions work but rsync (D) for file synchronization is fragile and doesn't scale.

stem: A company needs to ensure that all data transfers between its AWS accounts and the internet are inspected for malware and data exfiltration. The company has 30 VPCs across 10 accounts. All internet-bound traffic must pass through a centralized inspection point. On-premises traffic must bypass inspection. Which architecture implements centralized internet traffic inspection?

options.text: Deploy NAT gateways in each VPC individually, install host-based IDS agents on all EC2 instances, and use VPC Flow Logs with Lambda to detect data exfiltration patterns in traffic.
Deploy AWS Network Firewall in a centralized inspection VPC, configure Transit Gateway routing to direct all internet-bound traffic through the firewall VPC before reaching the NAT gateway.
Deploy third-party firewall appliances on EC2 in each VPC, route internet traffic through local appliances using VPC route tables, and use a centralized management console for rule deployment.
Deploy AWS WAF on all internet-facing ALBs and API Gateways to inspect HTTP traffic, configure AWS Shield Advanced for DDoS protection, and enable CloudFront with field-level encryption.

explanation: Centralized Network Firewall in an inspection VPC with Transit Gateway routing ensures all internet-bound traffic passes through one inspection point. On-premises traffic routes directly through Transit Gateway without hitting the firewall. Per-VPC NAT gateways with host-based IDS (B) doesn't centralize inspection. WAF (C) only inspects HTTP traffic at L7, not all internet traffic. Per-VPC firewall appliances (D) don't centralize inspection and multiply management overhead.

stem: A company is designing an application that needs to handle both synchronous API requests and asynchronous background processing. The API processes 5,000 requests per second, and 20% of requests trigger long-running background jobs that take 5-15 minutes. The application must acknowledge API requests within 500ms regardless of whether a background job is needed. Which architecture meets these requirements?

options.text: Use API Gateway with Lambda for synchronous API processing, publish background job requests to SQS, and process background jobs with a separate Lambda consuming from the SQS queue.
Use API Gateway with Step Functions synchronous express workflows for all requests, configure wait states for background jobs up to 15 minutes, and return results upon completion.
Use ALB with ECS Fargate tasks for all request processing, implement background jobs as separate threads within the same container, and use ECS Service Auto Scaling.
Use API Gateway with Lambda for all processing, configure Lambda timeout to 15 minutes for background jobs, and use Lambda Destinations to route completed job results to SNS.

explanation: Lambda handles the synchronous API response within 500ms. SQS decouples background jobs, allowing immediate acknowledgement. Separate Lambda consumers process long-running jobs independently. This cleanly separates sync and async workloads. Lambda with 15-minute timeout (B) would block the API response for the full job duration. Background threads in containers (C) couple sync and async scaling, and threads may be lost on container recycling. Step Functions synchronous express (D) would make API callers wait for background job completion.

stem: A company has a data lake on S3 with data shared across multiple teams. The data steward team needs to grant fine-grained access to specific columns and rows of data in the data lake. Currently, access is controlled through S3 bucket policies and IAM policies, which cannot provide column-level or row-level security. Which solution provides the required fine-grained access control?

options.text: Implement AWS Lake Formation with data filters that define column-level and row-level permissions, register S3 data locations in Lake Formation, and grant access through the Lake Formation console.
Create Athena views per team that select only authorized columns with WHERE clauses for row filtering, grant Athena named query execution permissions, and restrict direct S3 access.
Create separate S3 prefixes per team with copies of data containing only the allowed columns, use Lambda to transform and copy data when the source changes, and control access via bucket policies.
Deploy Apache Ranger on EMR for data access control, define column and row level policies in Ranger, and require all data access to go through EMR clusters with Ranger enforcement.

explanation: Lake Formation provides native column-level and row-level security through data filters. It integrates with Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and Glue, enforcing access consistently. Registration of S3 locations centralizes governance. Copying data per team (B) creates data duplication and synchronization challenges. Apache Ranger on EMR (C) adds operational overhead and limits access to EMR only. Athena views (D) can be bypassed with direct S3 access and don't enforce security at the storage level.

stem: A company has a legacy application running on bare metal servers that uses raw block storage devices for high-performance data processing. The application requires direct block-level access to storage with consistent sub-millisecond I/O latency. The company is migrating to EC2 but needs to maintain the same storage performance characteristics. Which storage configuration provides equivalent block-level performance?

options.text: Use Amazon EBS io2 Block Express volumes with provisioned IOPS up to 256,000 and throughput up to 4,000 MB/s, attached to a Nitro-based EC2 instance for maximum performance.
Use Amazon S3 with the S3 Express One Zone storage class for single-digit millisecond access latency, mounting S3 as a local filesystem using s3fs-fuse for block-level access.
Use Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with SSD storage tier configured for maximum IOPS, mount iSCSI LUNs from the ONTAP system to provide block-level storage access to EC2.
Use Amazon EFS with Provisioned Throughput mode configured for maximum throughput, and mount the file system using the EFS mount helper with recommended NFS mount options.

explanation: EBS io2 Block Express provides the highest block-level storage performance with sub-millisecond latency, up to 256K IOPS, and 4,000 MB/s throughput. Nitro instances maximize the EBS bandwidth. S3 Express One Zone (B) is object storage, not block storage, and s3fs-fuse adds overhead and doesn't provide true block-level access. EFS (C) is network file storage with higher latency than local block storage. FSx for ONTAP iSCSI (D) adds network overhead reducing performance below what direct EBS attachment provides.

stem: A company needs to manage AWS costs across 100 accounts in an Organization. Each account is owned by a different department. The finance team needs to allocate shared infrastructure costs (like Transit Gateway and shared VPC NAT gateways) proportionally to the departments that use them. Which approach enables accurate cost allocation of shared resources?

options.text: Enable AWS Billing Conductor with pricing rules to create custom line items that split shared infrastructure costs across accounts based on configurable allocation percentages per department.
Use AWS Cost Explorer cost allocation tags to tag shared resources with a 'SharedInfra' tag, create custom cost categories in Cost Explorer to split shared costs by department usage ratios.
Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) delivered to S3, build a custom cost allocation model in Athena that queries CUR data and distributes shared costs based on usage metrics per account.
Configure AWS Budgets for each department with budget amounts that include their estimated share of shared infrastructure costs, and adjust manually at the end of each quarter.

explanation: AWS Billing Conductor creates custom billing groups with pricing rules that allocate shared costs proportionally across accounts. It provides departments with bills reflecting their true cost including shared infrastructure allocation. Cost allocation tags (A) tag resources but cannot split a single resource's cost across multiple departments. Custom CUR analysis (B) requires building and maintaining complex ETL pipelines. Manual budget adjustments (D) are error-prone and not scalable.

stem: A company is building a recommendation engine for its e-commerce platform. The engine must serve personalized product recommendations with sub-100ms latency for 50 million users. Recommendations must update based on real-time user behavior (clicks, purchases, cart adds). The company has a data science team but wants to minimize infrastructure management. Which architecture should the architect recommend?

options.text: Pre-compute recommendations for all users using EMR Spark, store results in DynamoDB, update recommendations in nightly batch jobs, and serve from DynamoDB with DAX caching.
Use Amazon Personalize for real-time recommendations with event tracking for user interactions, deploy a Personalize campaign with auto-scaling, and integrate via API with the application.
Deploy Apache Mahout on EMR for collaborative filtering, store user-item interaction matrices in Redis, compute real-time recommendations on request, and cache results in CloudFront.
Deploy a custom recommendation model on SageMaker real-time endpoints with auto-scaling, use Kinesis Data Streams for real-time event ingestion, and retrain the model hourly on SageMaker.

explanation: Amazon Personalize provides managed real-time recommendation with built-in event tracking for user behavior updates. It handles model training, hosting, and scaling automatically. Sub-100ms inference latency meets the requirement. Custom SageMaker (B) requires more infrastructure management for training, hosting, and event processing pipelines. Pre-computed batch recommendations (C) don't reflect real-time user behavior. Apache Mahout on EMR (D) is outdated and requires significant infrastructure management.

stem: A company uses AWS Secrets Manager to store database credentials for 50 applications. The security team discovered that most credentials have not been rotated in over a year, and some applications use hard-coded credentials that don't reference Secrets Manager at all. The company wants to enforce automatic rotation and eliminate hard-coded credentials. Which approach addresses both issues?

options.text: Enable automatic rotation on all Secrets Manager secrets with 30-day intervals, deploy AWS Config rules to detect hard-coded credentials in code repositories using custom Lambda checks.
Create an SCP denying the ability to use long-lived database credentials, configure Secrets Manager rotation with Lambda rotation functions, and use Amazon CodeGuru for static analysis.
Migrate all applications to use IAM database authentication instead of passwords, eliminating the need for credential rotation entirely, and use Secrets Manager only for non-database secrets.
Enable automatic rotation on all secrets, use Amazon Inspector to scan application deployments for hard-coded credentials, and create CloudWatch alarms for secrets exceeding rotation age.

explanation: Automatic rotation with 30-day intervals ensures credentials are regularly rotated. AWS Config custom rules can scan for hard-coded credentials in deployment configurations and code. Together these enforce rotation and detect bypass. SCPs (B) cannot control database credential usage at the application level. Inspector (C) scans for vulnerabilities, not hard-coded application credentials. IAM database authentication (D) is limited to Aurora and RDS MySQL/PostgreSQL and requires significant application changes.

stem: A company runs a large Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) application on-premises. The application has complex integrations with other on-premises systems and customized Oracle forms. The company wants to move to AWS while continuing to run Oracle EBS. The database is 5 TB with peak usage of 30,000 IOPS. Which migration strategy should the architect recommend?

options.text: Modernize Oracle EBS by replacing it with SAP S/4HANA on AWS, migrating customizations to the SAP platform, and deploying on HANA-certified EC2 instances for improved performance.
Lift-and-shift Oracle EBS to EC2 instances with RDS for Oracle as the database, using io2 EBS volumes for the application tier and DMS for database migration with minimal downtime.
Migrate Oracle EBS to EC2 instances with the Oracle database running on EC2 using io2 Block Express EBS volumes provisioned for 30,000 IOPS, and use RMAN for database migration.
Containerize Oracle EBS components on EKS, migrate the database to Aurora PostgreSQL using SCT and DMS, and refactor Oracle Forms as React-based web applications on Amplify.

explanation: Oracle EBS requires the Oracle database with specific features that RDS for Oracle may not support fully (like Oracle RAC or specific PL/SQL packages). Running the database on EC2 provides full control. io2 Block Express handles 30K IOPS. RMAN provides native Oracle backup and restore. RDS for Oracle (A) may lack required EBS-specific database features. Replacing with SAP (C) is a completely different application, not a migration. Containerizing EBS and converting to Aurora/React (D) would be an enormous rewrite effort.

stem: A company operates in a highly regulated industry and must demonstrate compliance with multiple frameworks including SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA. The company needs continuous evidence collection from 40 AWS accounts, automated control assessments, and audit-ready report generation. Manual evidence collection currently takes 3 months per audit cycle. Which solution automates compliance evidence collection?

options.text: Deploy AWS Security Hub with compliance standards enabled, use the CIS and PCI DSS built-in standards as proxies for SOC 2 and ISO 27001, and export findings for audit reports.
Deploy AWS Audit Manager with pre-built assessment frameworks for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA, enable continuous evidence collection across all accounts, and generate assessment reports.
Create custom CloudWatch dashboards showing security metrics mapped to each compliance framework control, export dashboard data monthly, and compile evidence packages manually.
Use AWS Config conformance packs mapped to each compliance framework, aggregate findings in a central account, and generate custom reports using Athena queries against Config data.

explanation: Audit Manager provides pre-built frameworks for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA with automated evidence collection from AWS services across accounts. It generates audit-ready assessment reports directly. Config conformance packs (B) help with technical controls but don't map to full compliance frameworks or generate audit reports. Security Hub (C) doesn't have SOC 2 or ISO 27001 standards and its standards don't provide full framework coverage. Custom dashboards (D) still require manual evidence compilation.

stem: A company is designing a high-performance computing (HPC) cluster for computational fluid dynamics simulations. Each simulation requires 1,000 CPU cores communicating via MPI (Message Passing Interface) with low-latency interconnect. Simulations run for 48-72 hours. The company runs 2-3 simulations per week and wants to minimize costs when the cluster is idle. Which architecture optimizes for both performance and cost?

options.text: Use AWS ParallelCluster to create an HPC cluster with c6i.metal instances in a cluster placement group, Elastic Fabric Adapter for MPI, and auto-scaling to zero when no jobs are queued.
Deploy EC2 Spot Instances with a diversified fleet strategy across multiple instance types and AZs, configure EFA for low-latency networking, and use a Slurm scheduler on a head node.
Deploy a fixed-size EKS cluster with c6i.24xlarge instances across three AZs, use the MPI Operator for job submission, and keep the cluster running permanently for availability.
Use AWS Batch with Fargate for submitting simulation jobs, configure multi-node parallel jobs with 1000 vCPUs, and use S3 for input/output data staging between job submissions.

explanation: ParallelCluster manages the HPC cluster lifecycle including auto-scaling to zero when idle, eliminating costs between simulations. Cluster placement groups with EFA provide the low-latency MPI interconnect required. c6i.metal instances provide the raw CPU performance. A permanently running EKS cluster (B) wastes money during idle periods. Fargate (C) doesn't support EFA or cluster placement groups needed for MPI. Spot Instances (D) risk interruption during 48-72 hour simulations, causing job failures.

stem: A company has a distributed application that experiences intermittent performance issues. The team suspects the problem is related to the interaction between several microservices, but traditional monitoring with CloudWatch metrics and logs hasn't identified the bottleneck. The team needs to understand request flows and identify where latency is introduced across the service chain. Which observability approach helps identify the bottleneck?

options.text: Add detailed logging with timestamps at the entry and exit of each microservice, centralize logs in CloudWatch Logs, and manually calculate latency differences between service timestamps.
Configure CloudWatch Synthetics canaries to simulate user requests at regular intervals, monitor canary latency metrics, and create CloudWatch dashboards correlating canary data with service health.
Implement AWS X-Ray tracing across all microservices, enable X-Ray sampling at 100% for debugging, use the X-Ray service map to visualize latency distribution and identify bottleneck services.
Enable VPC Flow Logs on all subnets, analyze network latency between services using Athena queries on flow log data, and identify if the bottleneck is network-related between services.

explanation: X-Ray provides distributed tracing that follows requests across microservices, showing exactly where latency is introduced. The service map visualizes latencies and error rates between services. 100% sampling during debugging captures all problematic requests. Manual log correlation (B) is time-consuming and error-prone for distributed requests. VPC Flow Logs (C) show network traffic but not application-level latency within services. Synthetics canaries (D) detect issues from the outside but don't reveal internal service-to-service latency distribution.

stem: A company runs an on-premises MySQL 5.7 database that supports both transactional and reporting workloads. The database has 2 TB of data and uses stored procedures, triggers, and views extensively. The company wants to migrate to an Aurora MySQL cluster while adding read scalability for reporting. The migration must have less than 4 hours of downtime. Which migration approach meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a mysqldump of the database, upload to S3, restore to Aurora MySQL using the S3 import feature, manually recreate stored procedures and triggers, and add reader instances afterward.
Use AWS Snowball to transfer the 2 TB database export to S3, restore from S3 to Aurora MySQL, set up DMS CDC for any changes made during the transfer, and cut over when synchronized.
Use AWS DMS with a full load and CDC replication task from on-premises MySQL to Aurora MySQL, add Aurora reader instances for reporting, and cut over during the CDC catch-up phase.
Set up native MySQL binary log replication from on-premises to Aurora MySQL as an external replica, promote Aurora to standalone when replication lag is minimal, and add reader instances.

explanation: Native MySQL binary log replication preserves all stored procedures, triggers, and views during replication to Aurora. Promotion to standalone happens when lag is minimal, minimizing downtime. Reader instances add reporting scalability. DMS (A) may not replicate all MySQL-specific objects like triggers and stored procedures. mysqldump (B) requires downtime for the dump/restore cycle and manual recreation of database objects. Snowball (C) is overkill for 2 TB and adds unnecessary complexity.

stem: A company is deploying workloads to AWS GovCloud for FedRAMP compliance. The company also has commercial workloads in standard AWS Regions. The company needs connectivity between GovCloud and commercial Regions for data sharing while maintaining the security boundaries required by FedRAMP. Which architecture enables this cross-partition connectivity?

options.text: Use VPC peering between GovCloud VPCs and commercial Region VPCs to establish direct network connectivity, and apply security groups to control the allowed data flows between them.
Deploy Transit Gateway in both partitions and create a cross-partition Transit Gateway peering connection to route traffic between GovCloud and commercial VPCs using AWS backbone.
Establish a VPN connection between VPCs in GovCloud and commercial Regions using EC2-based VPN endpoints in both partitions, encrypting all traffic with customer-managed certificates.
Use AWS PrivateLink to create cross-partition endpoint services, exposing specific services from GovCloud as endpoints in the commercial partition for controlled data access.

explanation: GovCloud and commercial AWS are separate partitions with no native cross-partition networking. EC2-based VPN endpoints in both partitions with encrypted tunnels over the internet provide connectivity while maintaining security boundaries. VPC peering (B) does not work across AWS partitions (GovCloud and commercial). Transit Gateway peering (C) does not support cross-partition peering. PrivateLink (D) does not work across partitions.

stem: A company is designing a data mesh architecture where each business domain team owns and publishes its data products. The architecture must support data product discovery, quality enforcement, access control across domains, and lineage tracking. Which TWO AWS services are essential for implementing data mesh governance?

options.text: Amazon Redshift Serverless for querying all data products through a single unified endpoint, using cross-database queries to access data products stored in different team schemas.
AWS Glue Data Catalog for data product registration and discovery, schema management, and data lineage tracking through Glue ETL job relationships and crawled metadata updates.
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for real-time data product publishing, enabling downstream teams to subscribe to data product changes as streaming events with exactly-once delivery.
AWS Lake Formation for centralized access control with fine-grained permissions, cross-account data sharing through data catalog resource policies, and automatic data classification.

explanation: Lake Formation provides centralized access control and cross-account data sharing essential for data mesh governance. Glue Data Catalog provides data product discovery, schema management, and lineage tracking needed for data mesh discoverability. Redshift Serverless (C) is a query engine, not a governance tool for data mesh. Kinesis (D) is for streaming but doesn't provide data product discovery, quality enforcement, or access control governance.

stem: A company runs a critical application behind an Application Load Balancer. The application is experiencing occasional spikes in 5xx errors during deployments and scaling events. The ALB health checks are configured with a 30-second interval and a healthy threshold of 5, meaning it takes 2.5 minutes before new instances receive traffic. This causes existing instances to be overloaded during scale-out. Which optimization reduces the time for new instances to start receiving traffic?

options.text: Reduce the ALB health check interval to 5 seconds with a healthy threshold of 2, configure a lightweight health check endpoint, and enable slow start mode on the target group.
Enable cross-zone load balancing on the ALB to distribute traffic more evenly, increase the deregistration delay to allow draining connections, and configure connection idle timeout.
Increase the number of instances in the Auto Scaling group minimum capacity to reduce the need for scale-out events, and configure scheduled scaling for known peak traffic periods.
Replace the ALB with an NLB which performs faster health checks at the TCP level, configure a 5-second health check interval, and use target group IP-based routing for faster registration.

explanation: Reducing health check interval and threshold makes instances healthy in 10 seconds instead of 2.5 minutes. A lightweight health check endpoint ensures fast responses. Slow start mode gradually increases traffic to new instances, preventing overload. NLB (B) loses L7 features needed for the application and TCP health checks may not validate application readiness. Higher minimum capacity (C) increases costs without fixing the health check timing issue. Cross-zone load balancing (D) helps distribution but doesn't address the registration delay.

stem: A company is modernizing an application by moving from synchronous REST API calls between services to an event-driven architecture. The current architecture has tight coupling where the order service synchronously calls inventory, payment, and shipping services in sequence. A failure in any service causes the entire order to fail. Which event-driven pattern decouples the services while ensuring all steps complete reliably?

options.text: Publish order events to an SNS topic with SQS subscriptions for each service, process events independently in each service, and use DLQs to capture and retry failures for each consumer.
Implement the saga pattern using Step Functions orchestration, where each service step has a compensating transaction, and failures trigger rollback of previously completed steps automatically.
Implement the saga pattern using choreography with EventBridge, where each service publishes completion events that trigger the next service, and failure events trigger compensating actions.
Replace synchronous REST calls with SQS queues between services in a chain, where each service sends the result to the next service's queue, maintaining the sequential processing order.

explanation: Step Functions orchestrated saga provides centralized workflow management with built-in compensation logic. Each step has a corresponding rollback step, and Step Functions handles failure detection and compensation automatically. This ensures all steps complete or all are rolled back. SNS/SQS fanout (B) processes independently but doesn't coordinate the saga or handle rollback. Choreographed saga (C) distributes coordination complexity making debugging harder. SQS chaining (D) maintains tight coupling in an asynchronous form without compensation.

stem: A company needs to provide a secure, auditable mechanism for partners to upload large files (up to 5 GB) to specific S3 buckets in partner-dedicated prefixes. Partners should not be able to list, read, or delete any objects. Each upload must be virus-scanned before the file becomes available for internal processing. Which architecture implements secure partner file upload?

options.text: Create a public S3 bucket with a bucket policy allowing PutObject from partner IP ranges, enable versioning for audit trails, and configure S3 Object Lambda for virus scanning on read.
Deploy AWS Transfer Family with SFTP endpoints for each partner, configure S3 as the backend storage with partner-scoped home directories, and integrate with a virus scanning solution.
Generate S3 pre-signed URLs with PutObject-only permissions scoped to partner prefixes, trigger Lambda on upload to scan with ClamAV, and move clean files to a processing bucket.
Create IAM users per partner with policies allowing only s3:PutObject on their prefix, provide access keys for programmatic upload, and use S3 event notifications for virus scanning.

explanation: AWS Transfer Family provides managed SFTP endpoints familiar to partners, with S3 backend storage. Partner-scoped home directories restrict access to their prefix. Integration with virus scanning can be automated. Pre-signed URLs (A) work but require partner integration with AWS SDK and have expiration challenges for large files. IAM users per partner (B) require credential management and rotation for external entities. Public bucket with IP restrictions (D) is insecure as IP ranges can change and public buckets violate security best practices.

stem: A company is designing a graph-based fraud detection system. The system must store relationships between entities (users, devices, IP addresses, transactions) and traverse these relationships to identify fraud patterns like shared devices across accounts or velocity of transactions from the same IP. Queries must complete within 100 milliseconds. Which database is most suitable for this graph-based fraud detection?

options.text: Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with recursive CTEs for graph traversal queries, create indexes on relationship columns, and use read replicas for distributing analytical query load.
Use Amazon OpenSearch with nested document types for modeling entity relationships, implement graph-like queries using aggregations and script scoring for pattern matching across entities.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with adjacency list patterns for modeling graph relationships, implement graph traversal logic in Lambda functions, and use DAX for caching frequent queries.
Use Amazon Neptune with Gremlin queries for graph traversal, deploy a multi-AZ cluster with read replicas for query scaling, and use Neptune ML for pattern detection in the graph.

explanation: Neptune is purpose-built for graph data with optimized storage and query execution for graph traversals. Gremlin provides expressive graph queries for fraud pattern detection. Neptune ML adds machine learning-based pattern detection. Multi-AZ and read replicas ensure performance. DynamoDB adjacency lists (B) require multiple queries for deep traversals, and graph logic in Lambda adds latency. PostgreSQL recursive CTEs (C) perform poorly on deep graph traversals compared to native graph databases. OpenSearch (D) is a search engine, not optimized for graph traversal operations.

stem: A company runs a data pipeline that uses Glue ETL jobs to transform data from S3 and load it into Redshift. The pipeline has become unreliable with frequent job failures due to data quality issues in source files. Bad records cause entire jobs to fail, requiring manual intervention to identify and skip the problematic records. The company needs to make the pipeline more resilient to data quality issues. Which improvement addresses this requirement?

options.text: Increase Glue job retry attempts to 5 with exponential backoff, add a try-catch block in the Glue script to log errors, and continue processing the remaining records after each failure.
Add Glue DataBrew data quality rules as a pre-processing step to validate source files before ETL, quarantine files that fail validation to a separate S3 prefix, and alert the data team.
Replace Glue ETL with Lambda functions that process S3 files line-by-line, skip any records that fail parsing, write valid records to Redshift, and log skipped records to CloudWatch.
Configure Redshift COPY command with MAXERROR parameter to tolerate a specified number of load errors, allowing the data load to complete even with some invalid records in source files.

explanation: DataBrew data quality rules as a pre-processing step catch issues before they reach the ETL pipeline. Quarantining bad files prevents downstream failures while alerting enables investigation. This is a proactive approach. Retries with error handling (B) still process bad data and may not handle all failure modes. Lambda line-by-line processing (C) is inefficient for large datasets and doesn't validate data systematically. Redshift MAXERROR (D) skips errors silently during load but doesn't address ETL transformation failures.

stem: A company is migrating a suite of 20 interdependent applications from on-premises to AWS. The applications have complex dependencies, and the migration team needs to determine the correct migration order. Some applications must be migrated together as a group due to tight integration. The company has already completed discovery using AWS Application Discovery Service. Which tool helps determine the optimal migration wave plan?

options.text: Use AWS CloudFormation to model the target architecture for all applications, deploy them simultaneously in AWS, and resolve dependency issues post-migration through configuration updates.
Export Application Discovery Service data to a spreadsheet, manually map dependencies between applications, and create a migration wave plan based on the team's knowledge of the systems.
Use AWS Migration Hub with the Strategy Recommendations feature to analyze discovered data, group applications by dependencies, and generate recommended migration wave plans with priorities.
Use AWS Application Migration Service to create replication jobs for all servers, test each migration independently in an isolated VPC, and determine the order based on test success rates.

explanation: Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations analyzes discovery data to automatically identify application groupings based on dependencies and recommends migration strategies and wave plans. This leverages the data already collected. Testing each migration independently (B) doesn't identify dependency groupings before migration. Manual spreadsheet analysis (C) is error-prone for complex dependencies across 20 applications. Simultaneous deployment (D) risks dependency failures and is a high-risk big-bang approach.

stem: A company needs to centrally manage and rotate SSH keys used to access EC2 instances across 50 accounts. Currently, each team manages their own key pairs, leading to untracked keys and former employees potentially retaining access. The company wants to eliminate SSH key management entirely while maintaining secure shell access with full session logging. Which solution replaces SSH key management?

options.text: Deploy EC2 Instance Connect across all accounts, generate one-time SSH keys for each connection request, configure security groups to allow SSH from company IP ranges only for access.
Use AWS Secrets Manager to store SSH private keys with automatic rotation, deploy a custom script that retrieves keys before each SSH connection, and audit key usage via CloudTrail.
Deploy AWS Systems Manager Session Manager across all accounts, disable SSH ports in security groups, use IAM policies for access control, and log all sessions to CloudWatch Logs and S3.
Deploy a centralized SSH bastion host in a shared services account, manage authorized_keys files centrally, rotate keys monthly using Lambda, and log SSH sessions using script command.

explanation: Session Manager eliminates SSH keys entirely by providing browser and CLI-based shell access using IAM authentication. Disabling SSH ports removes the key management surface. Full session logging to CloudWatch and S3 provides audit trails. Centralized bastion (B) still requires SSH key management. Secrets Manager for SSH keys (C) still uses keys, adding complexity rather than eliminating them. EC2 Instance Connect (D) still requires SSH port access and generates temporary keys rather than eliminating key-based access.

stem: A company needs to deploy a PostgreSQL database that supports up to 128 TB of storage, automatic scaling of both compute and storage, and must handle unpredictable traffic patterns ranging from near-zero to thousands of transactions per second. The database must also support PostgreSQL extensions for PostGIS geospatial queries. Which database deployment option best meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL provisioned cluster with Auto Scaling reader instances, configure storage auto-scaling up to 128 TB, and enable PostGIS extension on all instances.
Deploy Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 with PostgreSQL compatibility, configure minimum and maximum ACU capacity, and enable the PostGIS extension for geospatial query capabilities.
Deploy PostgreSQL on EC2 with EBS auto-scaling, configure an Auto Scaling group with multiple PostgreSQL replicas behind an NLB, and install PostGIS from the official repository.
Deploy Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with Multi-AZ and storage auto-scaling, configure a db.r6g.16xlarge instance to handle peak traffic, and enable the PostGIS extension on the cluster.

explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 automatically scales compute (ACUs) based on demand from near-zero to high throughput, handles unpredictable traffic patterns, supports up to 128 TB storage, and supports PostgreSQL extensions including PostGIS. RDS with fixed instance (B) doesn't scale compute automatically for unpredictable traffic. Aurora provisioned (C) scales readers but the writer remains fixed-size. EC2-based PostgreSQL (D) requires manual compute scaling and adds significant operational overhead.

stem: A company hosts multiple websites behind CloudFront distributions. The security team has identified a pattern of credential stuffing attacks targeting login pages across multiple sites. The attacks use distributed botnets that rotate IP addresses frequently, making IP-based blocking ineffective. The company needs automated protection that adapts to evolving attack patterns. Which solution provides the most effective defense?

options.text: Implement CAPTCHA on all login pages using a third-party service, configure CloudFront to require signed cookies for login page access, and use Lambda@Edge to validate CAPTCHA responses.
Configure CloudFront geographic restrictions to block traffic from countries where the company doesn't operate, and add rate-limiting rules in AWS WAF based on IP address request frequency.
Deploy AWS Shield Advanced on all CloudFront distributions for DDoS protection, configure proactive engagement with the Shield Response Team, and use Shield Advanced cost protection.

Deploy AWS WAF with Bot Control managed rule group on all CloudFront distributions, enable targeted bot mitigation for login pages, and configure token-based challenge actions for suspicious requests.

explanation: WAF Bot Control uses machine learning to detect and mitigate bot traffic including credential stuffing. Token-based challenges (CAPTCHA/silent challenge) adapt to evolving attack patterns. It works across distributed botnets that rotate IPs. Geographic restrictions (B) block legitimate users and don't stop attacks from allowed countries. Shield Advanced (C) is for DDoS, not credential stuffing. Third-party CAPTCHA with signed cookies (D) adds complexity and doesn't adaptively detect bots.

stem: A company is migrating an on-premises SAP S/4HANA system with a 4 TB HANA database to AWS. The system requires high memory instances for the HANA database and specific storage performance characteristics. The company needs to maintain SAP support and certification. Which migration approach ensures SAP certification compliance on AWS?

options.text: Deploy SAP HANA on Aurora PostgreSQL with the HANA compatibility layer, migrate data using AWS DMS, and use the SAP ABAP adapter for Aurora to maintain application compatibility.
Deploy SAP HANA on Amazon RDS for SAP HANA managed service, configure Multi-AZ for high availability, and use automated backups with point-in-time recovery for data protection.
Deploy SAP HANA on SAP-certified EC2 instances (x2idn or u-series) with EBS io2 volumes provisioned according to SAP sizing guidelines, and use AWS Backint Agent for HANA backups to S3.
Deploy SAP HANA on standard memory-optimized EC2 instances (r6i.24xlarge) with gp3 EBS volumes, install HANA from SAP media, and configure AWS Backup for nightly database snapshots.

explanation: SAP-certified EC2 instances (x2idn, u-series) meet SAP HANA hardware requirements for certification and support. EBS io2 volumes meet SAP storage KPI requirements. AWS Backint Agent provides SAP-certified backup integration. Standard r6i instances (B) may not be SAP-certified for HANA and gp3 may not meet HANA storage KPIs. Aurora PostgreSQL (C) is not SAP HANA and there is no HANA compatibility layer. RDS for SAP HANA (D) does not exist as an AWS service.

stem: A company wants to prevent accidental deletion of critical CloudFormation stacks across all accounts in its Organization. The company also needs to ensure that production stacks can only be updated through the CI/CD pipeline and not through the AWS Console or CLI directly. Which combination of controls achieves this?

options.text: Use CloudFormation stack policies to deny Update:Delete actions on all resources, enable termination protection, and restrict console access using IAM policies in each member account.
Configure AWS Config rules to detect CloudFormation stack deletions, trigger auto-remediation to re-deploy deleted stacks from a backup, and alert the operations team via SNS notification.
Create IAM permission boundaries in each account that deny CloudFormation delete and update actions, attach boundaries to all IAM users and roles, and exempt the pipeline role explicitly.
Enable termination protection on all production stacks, create SCPs denying cloudformation:DeleteStack and cloudformation:UpdateStack except for the CI/CD pipeline role using conditions.

explanation: Termination protection prevents accidental deletion. SCPs with condition keys (aws:PrincipalArn) restricting CloudFormation operations to only the pipeline role ensure all changes go through CI/CD. SCPs apply across all accounts from the organization level. Stack policies (B) protect resources within stacks but don't prevent stack deletion or restrict who can perform updates. Permission boundaries (C) require per-account management and can be modified by account admins. Config rules (D) are reactive—stacks are already deleted before remediation.

stem: A company is building an application that needs to perform complex full-text search across 500 million documents with features including fuzzy matching, faceted search, autocomplete suggestions, and relevance scoring. The search must return results within 200 milliseconds. The documents are updated in near real-time from a DynamoDB source table. Which search architecture meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudSearch for managed search, configure index fields for text and faceted search, use CloudSearch auto-scaling, and sync data from DynamoDB using periodic Lambda batch jobs.
Use DynamoDB with Global Secondary Indexes designed for search patterns, implement fuzzy matching in Lambda with Levenshtein distance calculations, and cache results in ElastiCache.
Use Amazon OpenSearch Service with DynamoDB Streams feeding a Lambda function that indexes documents in near real-time, configure the cluster with dedicated master nodes and UltraWarm storage.
Use Amazon Kendra enterprise search with a DynamoDB data source connector, configure custom relevance tuning, and use Kendra's built-in NLU for understanding natural language queries.

explanation: OpenSearch provides all required search features: full-text search, fuzzy matching, faceted search, autocomplete, and relevance scoring at scale. DynamoDB Streams with Lambda enables near real-time indexing. Dedicated master nodes ensure cluster stability. Amazon Kendra (B) is designed for enterprise document search with NLU, but may not handle 500 million documents cost-effectively. CloudSearch (C) has scaling limitations for this volume and lacks some advanced features. DynamoDB with custom search logic (D) cannot efficiently support full-text search, fuzzy matching, or faceted search at scale.

stem: A company has an existing VPC with public and private subnets running production workloads. The VPC CIDR block is nearly exhausted with only 50 IP addresses remaining. The company needs to add 200 more instances but cannot modify the existing VPC CIDR or migrate workloads. How should the architect expand the available IP address space?

options.text: Resize the existing subnets by deleting and recreating them with larger CIDR ranges, migrating instances subnet by subnet during maintenance windows to the expanded subnets.
Convert existing instances to use IPv6 addresses to free up IPv4 space, enable dual-stack networking on the VPC, and deploy new instances using IPv6-only subnets to conserve addresses.
Create a new VPC with a larger CIDR block, establish VPC peering with the existing VPC, deploy new instances in the new VPC, and configure routing between both VPCs.
Add a secondary CIDR block to the existing VPC using a non-overlapping range, create new subnets in the secondary CIDR, and update route tables to include the new address space.

explanation: Secondary CIDR blocks can be added to existing VPCs without disruption. New subnets in the secondary CIDR provide additional IP addresses. Route tables automatically handle traffic within the VPC. No migration needed. New VPC with peering (B) adds complexity and doesn't extend the existing VPC's address space seamlessly. IPv6 (C) doesn't free IPv4 addresses and many applications don't support IPv6-only. Subnet resizing (D) requires deleting subnets which isn't possible while instances are running in them.

stem: A company runs a complex ETL pipeline using SSIS (SQL Server Integration Services) packages on-premises. The pipeline extracts data from multiple SQL Server databases, transforms it, and loads it into a data warehouse. The company is migrating to AWS and wants to modernize the ETL pipeline while maintaining the ability to handle complex transformations. Which approach replaces SSIS with the least disruption?

options.text: Rewrite all ETL logic as Apache Spark jobs running on Amazon EMR, read from RDS SQL Server using Spark JDBC connector, and write transformed data to S3 and then COPY to Redshift.
Use AWS Glue Studio for visual ETL design with Spark-based transformations, connect to RDS SQL Server sources using JDBC, and load transformed data into Redshift as the target warehouse.
Use AWS DMS to replicate data continuously from SQL Server sources to S3, then use Step Functions with Lambda to orchestrate transformation logic, and load results into Redshift.
Install SSIS on an EC2 Windows Server instance, maintain existing SSIS packages with minimal changes, connect to RDS SQL Server sources, and load data into Redshift using SSIS components.

explanation: Glue Studio provides a visual ETL designer similar to SSIS's visual paradigm, with Spark-based transformations handling complex logic. JDBC connectivity to SQL Server sources works natively. Redshift integration is built-in. This modernizes while maintaining ease of development. SSIS on EC2 (B) doesn't modernize the pipeline and maintains Windows Server management. DMS with Lambda (C) limits transformation complexity compared to SSIS capabilities. EMR Spark (D) requires code-heavy development without the visual design environment SSIS teams are accustomed to.

stem: A multinational company must comply with data sovereignty requirements where customer data from different countries must remain within those countries' borders. The company operates in the US, EU, and Japan. Application deployments must be identical across all regions, but data must never cross regional boundaries. Which architecture pattern enforces data sovereignty while maintaining consistent deployments?

options.text: Deploy the application in all three Regions with Aurora Global Database and write forwarding, partition data by country using application-level sharding within the shared global database.
Deploy identical application stacks in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-northeast-1 using StackSets, use separate databases per Region, and route users by country using Route 53 geolocation routing.
Deploy the application in us-east-1 only, use DynamoDB global tables with data tagged by country, implement application-level filtering to return only country-specific data per user request.
Deploy the application in us-east-1 with CloudFront in all regions for caching, encrypt country-specific data with region-specific KMS keys, and restrict key usage by geographic origin.

explanation: Separate application stacks per Region deployed via StackSets ensure consistency. Separate databases per Region enforce data sovereignty at the infrastructure level. Route 53 geolocation routing directs users to their country's Region. Single Region with global tables (B) replicates data globally, violating sovereignty. Aurora Global Database (C) replicates data across Regions even with application sharding. CloudFront caching in us-east-1 (D) processes all data in one Region, violating data sovereignty requirements.

stem: A company needs to implement a secrets management solution that supports automatic rotation of database credentials, API keys, and OAuth tokens. The solution must integrate with RDS, Redshift, and DocumentDB. Applications should retrieve secrets programmatically with caching to reduce API calls. The company also needs cross-Region secret replication for DR. Which solution meets all requirements?

options.text: Use HashiCorp Vault deployed on ECS Fargate with auto-unseal using KMS, configure dynamic database credentials for RDS, and deploy Vault replicas in each DR Region for availability.
Use AWS Certificate Manager for credential management, store API keys and OAuth tokens in encrypted DynamoDB Global Tables, and implement custom rotation logic in Step Functions workflows.
Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString parameters with KMS encryption, implement custom Lambda rotation functions, and use cross-Region parameter replication with EventBridge.
Use AWS Secrets Manager with native rotation Lambda functions for RDS, Redshift, and DocumentDB, enable multi-Region secret replication, and use the Secrets Manager caching client library.

explanation: Secrets Manager provides native rotation for RDS, Redshift, and DocumentDB without custom code. Multi-Region replication is built-in for DR. The caching client library reduces API calls. This is the most complete managed solution. Parameter Store (B) doesn't have native database rotation or built-in multi-Region replication. HashiCorp Vault (C) requires managing the Vault infrastructure. ACM (D) manages certificates not secrets, and DynamoDB with Step Functions requires building everything from scratch.

stem: A company runs an application that writes 50,000 records per second to a DynamoDB table. The table uses provisioned capacity mode with 50,000 WCU. During peak hours, the application experiences WriteThrottleEvents despite having sufficient provisioned capacity. Investigation reveals that all items have the same partition key prefix pattern causing hot partitions. Which change resolves the hot partition issue while maintaining write throughput?

options.text: Switch the table to on-demand capacity mode to leverage DynamoDB adaptive capacity, which automatically allocates more throughput to hot partitions without provisioned capacity management.
Create a DAX cluster in front of the DynamoDB table to absorb the write traffic, configure DAX write-through caching, and let DAX distribute writes across multiple DynamoDB partitions.
Redesign the partition key to distribute writes evenly by adding a random suffix or calculated hash to the current partition key, ensuring uniform distribution across all DynamoDB partitions.
Enable DynamoDB auto-scaling with a higher target utilization percentage of 90%, increase the maximum provisioned WCU to 100,000, and lower the scale-out cooldown period to respond faster.

explanation: Redesigning the partition key with random suffixes or calculated hashes distributes writes evenly across partitions, eliminating hot partitions. This addresses the root cause of uneven distribution. On-demand mode (A) provides adaptive capacity but doesn't solve extreme hot partition problems since individual partition limits still apply. Auto-scaling (C) adds more total capacity but doesn't redistribute the existing hot partition traffic. DAX (D) is a read cache and write-through doesn't solve partition-level write throttling.

stem: A company is migrating a high-availability Oracle RAC (Real Application Clusters) database to AWS. The database uses shared storage across multiple nodes for active-active clustering. The company needs similar high-availability characteristics with automatic failover and shared storage access. Which AWS database deployment provides the closest equivalent to Oracle RAC functionality?

options.text: Deploy Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with multiple writer instances in a multi-master configuration, using Aurora shared storage for data consistency across all writer nodes in the cluster.
Deploy Oracle on EC2 with multiple instances accessing shared EBS io2 Multi-Attach volumes in a cluster placement group, using Oracle Clusterware for RAC coordination between nodes.
Deploy Amazon RDS for Oracle Multi-AZ with synchronous replication to a standby instance, configure automatic failover, and use read replicas in other AZs for read scaling.
Deploy Amazon Aurora with a single writer and multiple reader instances across AZs, use Aurora Global Database for cross-Region availability, and configure automatic failover for the writer.

explanation: Aurora provides a shared storage architecture with automatic failover similar to RAC's high availability, though with a single writer. Aurora's storage is shared across all instances, providing the closest managed equivalent. Failover completes in seconds. Aurora multi-master (A) was deprecated. Oracle RAC on EC2 (B) is technically possible but EBS Multi-Attach has significant limitations for RAC shared storage requirements. RDS Oracle Multi-AZ (C) provides HA but the standby is not accessible for reads unlike RAC's active nodes.

stem: A company needs to implement centralized certificate management for TLS certificates used by applications across 30 accounts. Certificates must be automatically renewed before expiration, and the company needs visibility into all certificates nearing expiration across the organization. Private certificates for internal services must use a company-managed certificate authority. Which solution provides centralized certificate management?

options.text: Use ACM for public certificates with auto-renewal, ACM Private CA shared via RAM for private certificates, and AWS Config rules to detect certificates expiring within 30 days across accounts.
Use Let's Encrypt with Certbot on EC2 instances for automatic certificate renewal, store certificates in Secrets Manager with cross-account sharing, and monitor with CloudWatch custom metrics.
Deploy HashiCorp Vault on ECS for certificate management, use the Vault PKI secrets engine for both public and private certificates, and configure automatic renewal through Vault policies.
Purchase certificates from a third-party CA, import them into ACM in each account, create EventBridge rules to alert 30 days before expiration, and manually renew certificates per account.

explanation: ACM provides automatic renewal for public certificates. ACM Private CA with RAM sharing enables centralized private certificate management across accounts. AWS Config aggregator provides organization-wide visibility into certificate expiration. Third-party certificates (B) require manual renewal and per-account management. Let's Encrypt on EC2 (C) adds operational overhead and doesn't provide centralized management. HashiCorp Vault (D) requires infrastructure management and doesn't integrate natively with AWS services like ALB and CloudFront.

stem: A logistics company needs to optimize delivery routes for 10,000 vehicles in real-time, considering traffic conditions, delivery time windows, vehicle capacity constraints, and driver hours-of-service regulations. The optimization must run every 5 minutes with results returned within 2 minutes. This is a computationally intensive combinatorial optimization problem. Which compute architecture handles this workload?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker with a custom optimization model deployed on ml.p4d GPU instances, invoke the endpoint every 5 minutes from EventBridge, and return optimized routes via API Gateway.
Use Amazon Braket for quantum-inspired optimization algorithms that solve vehicle routing problems efficiently, submit optimization tasks through the Braket API on a 5-minute schedule.
Use AWS Lambda with 10 GB memory and 15-minute timeout to run the optimization algorithm, partition the 10,000 vehicles into smaller batches, and aggregate results from parallel executions.
Deploy the optimization solver on EC2 c6i.metal instances in a cluster placement group with EFA, use AWS Batch to submit optimization jobs every 5 minutes with a 2-minute timeout limit.

explanation: EC2 c6i.metal instances provide the raw compute power needed for combinatorial optimization. Cluster placement groups with EFA enable parallel computing for the solver. AWS Batch manages job scheduling with timeout enforcement. SageMaker (A) is designed for ML inference, not general combinatorial optimization solvers. Lambda (C) has memory and compute limitations unsuitable for large-scale optimization problems. Amazon Braket (D) is experimental for optimization problems and may not complete within 2 minutes for this problem size.

stem: A company has an existing API Gateway REST API with 200 endpoints. The company wants to implement API versioning to allow gradual migration of clients from v1 to v2 while maintaining backward compatibility. Some endpoints have changed in v2 while others remain identical. The company wants to minimize infrastructure duplication. Which versioning strategy minimizes resource duplication?

options.text: Create separate API Gateway deployments for v1 and v2 as stage variables, use a single set of Lambda functions with version routing logic based on the stage variable passed by API Gateway.
Create two completely separate API Gateway REST APIs for v1 and v2 with independent configurations, deploy separate Lambda functions for each version, and use custom domains with base path mapping.
Use a single API Gateway with path-based versioning (/v1/ and /v2/), create resources under each version path, point unchanged endpoints to the same Lambda function alias for both versions.
Use API Gateway request header-based versioning with a custom Accept-Version header, create Gateway responses that route to different Lambda function aliases based on the header value.

explanation: Path-based versioning (/v1/, /v2/) in a single API Gateway uses a single set of resources. Unchanged endpoints point to the same Lambda alias, avoiding duplication. Changed endpoints point to v2-specific functions. Stage variables (A) don't differentiate endpoints within a version well and require complex routing logic. Separate APIs (B) duplicates all 200 endpoints even when only some changed. Header-based routing (D) is complex to implement in API Gateway and harder for clients to use.

stem: A company is migrating a .NET application that uses Windows Authentication (NTLM/Kerberos) for single sign-on across multiple internal web applications. The applications are hosted on IIS on Windows Server. The company wants to maintain Windows Authentication while migrating to AWS. Which deployment architecture preserves Windows Authentication?

options.text: Containerize the .NET applications on ECS with Windows containers, configure Cognito User Pools for authentication, and replace Windows Authentication with OAuth 2.0 token-based flow.
Deploy the .NET applications on EC2 Windows instances joined to AWS Managed Microsoft AD, configure IIS with Windows Authentication, and use ALB with HTTPS listeners for load balancing.
Rewrite the .NET applications as .NET Core on Linux, deploy on ECS Fargate, implement OpenID Connect authentication with Cognito, and use ALB authentication integration.
Migrate the .NET applications to Elastic Beanstalk Windows platform, configure SAML-based authentication using IAM Identity Center, and remove the Windows Authentication dependencies.

explanation: EC2 Windows instances joined to Managed Microsoft AD support native Windows Authentication (NTLM/Kerberos) through IIS without application changes. ALB handles HTTPS termination. This preserves the existing auth mechanism. ECS with Cognito (B) replaces Windows Auth with OAuth, requiring application changes. SAML with IAM Identity Center (C) changes the authentication protocol. Rewriting to .NET Core on Linux (D) eliminates Windows Authentication capability entirely.

stem: A company's DevOps team needs to manage infrastructure deployments across 80 accounts with different configurations per account type (sandbox, development, staging, production). Each environment requires different instance sizes, security configurations, and retention policies. The team wants a single source of truth for infrastructure code with environment-specific parameters. Which deployment strategy provides this flexibility?

options.text: Use AWS CDK with environment-specific context values in cdk.json, define a single CDK app with conditional logic based on environment, and deploy using CDK Pipelines targeting account groups.
Create separate CloudFormation templates per environment type with hard-coded values, store templates in CodeCommit, and deploy using CodePipeline with environment-specific pipeline stages.
Use Terraform with workspace-based environment separation, store state files in S3 per workspace, and deploy using a Jenkins pipeline that selects the workspace based on target account type.
Use CloudFormation StackSets with parameter overrides per OU, define environment-specific parameters in a parameter file per OU, and deploy with StackSets targeting each OU separately.

explanation: CDK with context values provides a single codebase with environment-specific parameters. CDK Pipelines handles multi-account deployment with approval stages for production. Type-safe code catches errors before deployment. StackSets with parameter overrides (A) work but lack the type safety and reusability of CDK. Separate templates per environment (B) creates maintenance burden with duplicated code. Terraform workspaces (C) work but require Jenkins management and lack native AWS integration.

stem: A company is building a digital twin platform that ingests sensor data from 100,000 industrial IoT devices, creates virtual representations of physical assets, runs simulations against the digital models, and provides a 3D visualization dashboard. Each device sends data every second. Which architecture supports the complete digital twin pipeline?

options.text: Use Amazon Managed Grafana for dashboard visualization, IoT Greengrass for edge processing, DynamoDB for device state storage, and SageMaker for running simulation models against data.
Use a custom Unity3D application on EC2 GPU instances for 3D visualization, IoT Core for ingestion, Aurora PostgreSQL for sensor data storage, and Lambda for simulation processing.
Use AWS IoT SiteWise for industrial asset modeling, IoT Core for device management, S3 for raw data storage, and QuickSight for visualization dashboards with custom embedded analytics.
Use AWS IoT TwinMaker for digital twin modeling and visualization, IoT Core for device ingestion, Kinesis Data Streams for real-time processing, and Timestream for time-series sensor storage.

explanation: IoT TwinMaker provides purpose-built digital twin creation with 3D visualization, entity modeling, and scene composition. IoT Core handles device connections at scale. Kinesis processes real-time sensor streams. Timestream stores time-series data efficiently for 100K devices sending data every second. Grafana (B) provides dashboards but not digital twin modeling or 3D visualization. IoT SiteWise (C) provides asset modeling but lacks 3D digital twin visualization. Custom Unity3D (D) requires significant development and operational management.

stem: A company runs an application that uses Amazon Cognito for user authentication. The application has grown to 5 million users. The company notices that during password reset flows, some users' reset emails are delayed by up to 10 minutes. Investigation reveals that Cognito's built-in email delivery using Amazon SES sandbox mode has rate limits. Which solution resolves the email delivery delay?

options.text: Configure Cognito to use a verified SES identity in production mode as the email sender, request SES production access with higher sending quotas, and configure a custom FROM address.
Implement a custom message Lambda trigger in Cognito that sends emails through a third-party email provider like SendGrid, bypassing Cognito's built-in email delivery mechanism entirely.
Create a custom authentication flow that replaces email-based password reset with SMS-based verification using SNS, eliminating the dependency on email delivery for the password reset process.
Deploy a custom SES email receiving pipeline that pre-generates password reset tokens, caches them in ElastiCache, and serves tokens instantly when users request password resets.

explanation: Configuring Cognito to use SES production mode with higher sending quotas directly addresses the rate limiting issue. SES production access provides sufficient throughput for 5 million users. Custom FROM addresses improve deliverability. Custom Lambda trigger with third-party provider (B) adds complexity and external dependency when SES production mode solves the issue natively. SMS-based flow (C) changes the user experience and costs more per message. Pre-generated tokens (D) don't address the email delivery bottleneck.

stem: A company runs a legacy message-driven application that uses RabbitMQ as its message broker. The application relies on AMQP protocol features including message priority, dead-letter exchanges, and exchange-to-exchange binding. The company wants to migrate to a managed service while maintaining AMQP compatibility. Which target service should the architect recommend?

options.text: Migrate to Amazon SQS with SNS for fanout patterns, implement message priority using separate SQS queues per priority level, and use SQS dead-letter queues to replace dead-letter exchanges.
Migrate to Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ which supports AMQP alongside OpenWire, configure ActiveMQ exchanges and queues to match RabbitMQ behavior, and maintain AMQP client connections.
Migrate to Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ with a cluster deployment across multiple AZs, maintain existing AMQP connection strings with endpoint updates, and keep exchange and queue configurations.
Migrate to Amazon MSK (Managed Kafka), rewrite producers and consumers to use the Kafka protocol, implement priority with topic partitioning, and use Kafka DLQ topics for failed messages.

explanation: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ is a managed RabbitMQ service that supports all native AMQP features including message priority, dead-letter exchanges, and exchange bindings. Migration requires only endpoint changes. SQS/SNS (B) doesn't support AMQP protocol or RabbitMQ-specific features like exchange-to-exchange binding. MSK (C) uses a different protocol entirely. ActiveMQ (D) has a different exchange model than RabbitMQ despite AMQP support, requiring configuration changes.

stem: A company needs to implement a disaster recovery strategy for its entire AWS Organization consisting of 50 accounts. The DR plan must cover not just application workloads but also the organizational structure, SCPs, IAM roles, and network configurations. The company needs the ability to recreate the entire organization in a different partition if the primary fails. Which approach ensures comprehensive organizational DR?

options.text: Use AWS Organizations APIs to export the organizational structure programmatically, store exports in cross-Region S3 with versioning, and build automation to recreate the structure from exports.
Maintain a parallel AWS Organization with identical structure, sync SCPs and configurations using Lambda triggered by organizational change events, and keep both organizations active at all times.
Document all organizational configurations in version-controlled CloudFormation templates, store SCPs as code in CodeCommit, and maintain runbooks for manual reconstruction of the organization.
Implement infrastructure as code for the entire organization using AWS CDK with the Organizations construct library, store code in a DR-region CodeCommit repository, and test deployment quarterly.

explanation: CDK with Organizations constructs captures the entire organizational structure as code including OUs, SCPs, and account configurations. CodeCommit in the DR region ensures code availability. Quarterly testing validates the DR process. Manual documentation (A) is error-prone and becomes stale. API exports (B) capture point-in-time state but require building custom reconstruction automation. Parallel active organizations (D) doubles costs and complexity while creating synchronization challenges.

stem: A company is building a multi-player online game that requires a global leaderboard showing rankings in real-time. The leaderboard must support 10 million players, update within 1 second of a score change, and return the top 100 players or a player's rank within 10 milliseconds. Which data store and architecture supports this real-time leaderboard?

options.text: Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with a B-tree index on the score column, implement leaderboard queries using window functions for ranking, and deploy Aurora Global Database for multi-Region reads.
Use Amazon OpenSearch with a numeric score field, configure frequent index refreshes for near real-time updates, and use aggregation queries with top_hits for leaderboard ranking and display.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with a GSI on the score attribute for leaderboard queries, configure on-demand capacity for variable gaming traffic, and use DynamoDB Accelerator for sub-10ms reads.
