explanation: AWS Batch supports multiple compute environments with different instance types. Each job definition specifies exact resource requirements (CPU, memory, GPU). Job dependencies enforce step ordering. Batch provisions the right instance type for each step and terminates it after completion. Lambda (B) has a 15-minute timeout and 10 GB memory limit—insufficient for 256 GB RAM steps. Single large instance (C) wastes resources when steps need different hardware. EKS with Karpenter (D) requires managing Kubernetes infrastructure for batch workloads.

stem: A company's production workload runs on a fleet of 100 m5.2xlarge EC2 instances. Monitoring shows CPU utilization averages 15% with occasional spikes to 60%. The workload is compute-bound during spikes but memory utilization is consistently below 20% of the 32 GB available. The company wants to reduce costs while handling the CPU spikes. Which optimization reduces costs without impacting performance?

options.text: Right-size to m5.xlarge instances (half the size) and double the fleet to 200 instances behind a load balancer, maintaining the same total compute capacity but using smaller instances for flexibility.
Migrate to Graviton-based m6g.2xlarge instances for 20% cost savings with similar or better performance, maintain 100 instances for consistent capacity, and reserve instances for additional discount.
Right-size to c6i.xlarge instances (compute-optimized with 8 GB RAM) using 60 instances with target tracking auto-scaling on CPU at 60%, reducing base capacity while handling spikes with scaling.
Switch to t3.2xlarge burstable instances which provide the same 8 vCPUs and 32 GB RAM at lower cost, use CPU credits for handling spikes, and enable unlimited mode to prevent credit exhaustion.

explanation: The workload is compute-bound (not memory-bound) so compute-optimized c6i instances are appropriate. 8 GB RAM is sufficient given 20% utilization of 32 GB. Auto-scaling from a smaller base handles spikes without over-provisioning. This optimizes both instance family and fleet size. Burstable t3 (B) may exhaust credits during sustained spikes and unlimited mode can be expensive. m6g.2xlarge (C) saves 20% but still over-provisions memory and maintains 100 instances. Doubling to 200 m5.xlarge (D) doesn't reduce costs and adds operational complexity.

stem: A company wants to modernize its scheduled cron jobs that run on a Linux server. The server has 30 cron jobs with different schedules (hourly, daily, weekly). Jobs range from simple scripts (10 seconds) to complex data processing (45 minutes). Some jobs depend on the completion of other jobs. Which target architecture replaces the cron server with managed services?

options.text: Deploy a single EC2 instance with crontab configured identically to the on-premises server, use an Auto Scaling group of size 1 for availability, and monitor job execution via CloudWatch agent logs.
Use AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows for all job scheduling, run jobs as SSM Run Command documents on a managed EC2 instance, and configure maintenance window tasks for job dependencies.

Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler for cron schedules triggering Lambda for short jobs and ECS Fargate tasks for long-running jobs, orchestrate dependent jobs with Step Functions workflows for ordering.

Deploy all 30 jobs as Lambda functions with scheduled EventBridge rules, use Lambda Destinations for job dependency chaining, and configure Lambda provisioned concurrency for consistent startup latency.

explanation: EventBridge Scheduler handles cron expressions natively. Lambda suits short jobs (under 15 minutes) while ECS Fargate handles the 45-minute jobs. Step Functions orchestrates dependent jobs with conditional logic and error handling. This uses the right service for each job type. Single EC2 instance (B) doesn't modernize—it replicates the same problem in the cloud. SSM Maintenance Windows (C) are designed for patching, not general-purpose job scheduling. Lambda only (D) cannot handle 45-minute jobs due to the 15-minute timeout limit.

stem: A company needs to ensure that all API calls across their AWS Organization are logged, tamper-proof, and retained for 7 years for regulatory compliance. Logs must be centralized in a single account and individual account administrators must not be able to disable logging or delete log files. Which TWO configurations are required to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an Organization trail in CloudTrail from the management account, configure log delivery to an S3 bucket in a dedicated log archive account with Object Lock in Compliance mode and 7-year retention.

Enable CloudTrail Insights for anomaly detection across all accounts, configure CloudWatch Alarms for unauthorized API calls to CloudTrail and S3, and send alerts to the security team via SNS for investigation.

Create an SCP denying cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, s3:DeleteObject, and s3:PutBucketPolicy on the log archive bucket, applied to all OUs except the management account and log archive account.

Deploy individual CloudTrail trails in each account via StackSets, configure each trail to deliver to a central S3 bucket with versioning enabled, and use lifecycle policies to transition logs to Glacier after 90 days.

explanation: Organization trail provides centralized logging across all accounts from the management account. S3 Object Lock Compliance mode prevents deletion for 7 years and cannot be overridden. SCP denying CloudTrail and S3 delete operations prevents account administrators from disabling logging or deleting logs. Individual account trails (B) can be disabled by account admins and versioning alone doesn't prevent deletion. CloudTrail Insights (D) provides detection but doesn't prevent tampering or ensure retention.

stem: A company is designing an application that needs to process user-uploaded images through five independent ML models (object detection, face recognition, text extraction, scene classification, and sentiment analysis). Each model takes 2-5 seconds. Users expect results within 10 seconds of upload. Which architecture processes all models in parallel to meet the latency requirement?

options.text: Upload images to S3, trigger five separate Lambda functions via S3 event notification, each calling its SageMaker endpoint, write results to DynamoDB, and poll DynamoDB from the frontend for completion.

Use Step Functions Parallel state to invoke five Lambda functions simultaneously, each calling a separate SageMaker endpoint, aggregate results in a final Lambda state, and return combined results to the user.

Process images sequentially through each model using a single Lambda function that calls all five SageMaker endpoints one after another, accumulating results, then returning the combined output to the user.

Use SageMaker Inference Pipeline to chain all five models into a single endpoint, process each image through the pipeline sequentially, and return aggregated results from the pipeline's final container output.

explanation: Step Functions Parallel state invokes all five Lambda functions simultaneously. Each Lambda calls its SageMaker endpoint independently. With 2-5 seconds per model running in parallel, total time is 5-7 seconds (max model time + overhead). The final state aggregates results. Sequential processing (B) takes 10-25 seconds total, exceeding the requirement. S3 event with DynamoDB polling (C) adds latency from S3 notifications and polling delays. SageMaker Inference Pipeline (D) processes models sequentially, not in parallel.

stem: A company's Aurora MySQL cluster has a 2 TB database with read replicas handling read traffic. The company notices that during monthly reporting, a specific set of complex queries causes the read replicas to fall behind in replication lag, affecting real-time read traffic on the same replicas. Which approach isolates reporting queries from real-time read traffic?

options.text: Migrate reporting queries to Amazon Redshift using Aurora zero-ETL integration, run all complex reporting on Redshift while Aurora handles only OLTP reads, providing complete workload isolation between systems.

Implement application-level query routing using connection pooling with ProxySQL, tag queries as reporting or real-time, and route to different connection pools targeting the same read replicas with priority rules.

Create a custom Aurora endpoint routing reporting queries to dedicated larger reader instances, and a separate custom endpoint for real-time reads pointing to standard reader instances, isolating the workloads.

Schedule the monthly reporting to run during off-peak hours when real-time traffic is lowest, increase the instance size of all read replicas temporarily during reporting, and reduce instance size afterward.

explanation: Custom Aurora endpoints route queries to specific reader instances. Dedicated larger instances handle resource-intensive reports without affecting standard readers serving real-time traffic. This provides workload isolation within the same Aurora cluster. Off-peak scheduling (B) delays reporting and doesn't solve the problem if schedules overlap. ProxySQL routing (C) to the same replicas doesn't provide compute isolation. Redshift zero-ETL (D) is effective but adds cost and complexity for a monthly reporting use case that custom endpoints solve natively.

stem: A company is modernizing its session management for a web application. Currently sessions are stored on local file systems of individual web servers, causing session loss when servers are terminated during auto-scaling events. The application uses PHP and sessions contain user shopping cart data averaging 50 KB per session. Which session management solution eliminates session loss during scaling?

options.text: Deploy Amazon EFS and mount it on all web servers, configure PHP to use the EFS mount point as the session save path, allowing all servers to access the same session files on the shared file system.

Use ElastiCache for Redis with the PHP Redis session handler, configure Redis cluster mode for high availability, set session TTL to match application session timeout, and update PHP session configuration.

Store sessions in Amazon S3 using a custom PHP session handler, write session data as S3 objects keyed by session ID, configure S3 lifecycle rules for session expiration, and use S3 Standard storage class.

Enable sticky sessions on the Application Load Balancer using duration-based cookies, ensure users always route to the same server, and configure ASG to use connection draining with a long timeout before termination.

explanation: ElastiCache for Redis provides sub-millisecond session reads/writes, native PHP session handler integration, and data persistence across server changes. Redis cluster mode provides high availability. Session TTL handles automatic expiration. This is the standard pattern for PHP session externalization. Sticky sessions (B) still lose sessions when the target server terminates. S3 (C) has higher latency (100ms+) for session operations compared to Redis's sub-millisecond. EFS (D) uses file-based sessions with higher latency and file locking issues under concurrent access.

stem: A company's security policy requires that all S3 buckets across 200 accounts enforce encryption in transit (HTTPS only), block public access, and require server-side encryption. Currently there is no organization-wide enforcement, and new buckets are often created without these settings. Which preventive approach enforces S3 security baselines before buckets are used?

options.text: Create SCPs denying s3:CreateBucket unless aws:SecureTransport is true, denying s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock with public settings, and denying s3:PutObject without server-side encryption headers across all accounts.

Create IAM permission boundaries in each account that restrict S3 actions unless encryption and security conditions are met, deploy boundaries via StackSets, and attach to all IAM roles used for S3 access.

Enable S3 Block Public Access at the Organization level through the S3 console, create an SCP denying s3:PutObject unless encryption headers are present, and deploy bucket policies requiring HTTPS via StackSets.

Deploy AWS Config rules for s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only, s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited, and s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled, with automatic remediation Lambda functions in each account to fix non-compliant buckets.

explanation: Organization-level S3 Block Public Access prevents public bucket creation across all 200 accounts and cannot be overridden by account administrators. SCP denying PutObject without encryption headers enforces encryption at rest. StackSets bucket policies requiring HTTPS enforce encryption in transit. This covers all three requirements with preventive controls. SCPs denying CreateBucket (A) don't enforce settings on the bucket—they can only condition on request context. Config rules (C) are detective, not preventive. Permission boundaries (D) require attachment to every role and can be bypassed.

stem: A company is building a data pipeline that must process 1 million records per second from multiple Kafka topics, enrich each record with data from a reference table, perform windowed aggregations over 5-minute tumbling windows, and write results to multiple destinations (S3, Redshift, OpenSearch). Which architecture handles this stream processing at scale?

options.text: Use Amazon MSK for Kafka ingestion, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink for stream processing with enrichment and windowed aggregations, and Flink connectors for writing to S3, Redshift, and OpenSearch.

Deploy custom Spark Structured Streaming on EMR consuming from MSK, implement enrichment joins and windowed aggregations in Spark, and write outputs to S3, Redshift, and OpenSearch using Spark connectors.
Use Amazon MSK for ingestion, Lambda consumers for record processing with DynamoDB lookups for enrichment, SQS for buffering, and separate Lambda functions for writing to each destination system.

Use Kinesis Data Streams for ingestion, Kinesis Data Analytics SQL for windowed aggregations, Lambda for enrichment using Kinesis Analytics output, and Kinesis Data Firehose for S3 and Redshift delivery.

explanation: MSK handles Kafka topics natively. Managed Flink processes 1M records/sec with built-in windowed aggregations, enrichment via async I/O, and multiple sink connectors. Flink provides exactly-once semantics and handles complex stream processing. Lambda (B) cannot sustain 1M records/sec and has cold start issues. Kinesis Data Analytics SQL (C) has limited processing capabilities for complex enrichment. EMR Spark Streaming (D) requires managing cluster infrastructure.

stem: A company's application writes logs to CloudWatch Logs and metrics to CloudWatch Metrics. During incidents, engineers spend 30 minutes correlating logs, metrics, and traces across multiple dashboards to identify root causes. The mean time to resolution (MTTR) is 2 hours. Which approach reduces incident investigation time?

options.text: Implement AWS X-Ray for distributed tracing, use CloudWatch ServiceLens to correlate traces with logs and metrics in a single view, and create CloudWatch Application Signals for automated service health monitoring.

Create comprehensive CloudWatch dashboards combining all metrics and log widgets, add CloudWatch Anomaly Detection to all critical metrics, and configure composite alarms that aggregate multiple alarm states.

Increase CloudWatch Logs retention to 1 year for thorough post-incident analysis, create CloudWatch Contributor Insights rules for log pattern analysis, and document investigation procedures in runbooks.

Deploy a third-party APM solution like Datadog or New Relic, forward all CloudWatch logs and metrics to the APM platform, and use its AI-powered root cause analysis features for faster incident resolution.

explanation: X-Ray provides distributed tracing showing request flow and latencies. ServiceLens correlates traces with CloudWatch logs and metrics in a unified view, eliminating manual correlation. Application Signals provides automated service-level monitoring with health indicators. This directly reduces the 30-minute correlation time. Comprehensive dashboards (B) still require manual correlation between widgets. Third-party APM (C) adds cost and vendor dependency. Longer retention and runbooks (D) don't address the correlation problem.

stem: A company is migrating a file server with 50 TB of data and 500 million files from on-premises to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Users access files via SMB shares from Active Directory-joined workstations. The company needs to preserve all NTFS permissions, file metadata, and share configurations during migration. Which migration method preserves all Windows file system attributes?

options.text: Use AWS DataSync with an on-premises agent configured for SMB source and FSx for Windows destination, enable preservation of NTFS permissions and metadata, schedule transfer during off-peak hours for bandwidth.

Use Robocopy from an on-premises Windows server to copy files to the FSx share over Direct Connect, use the /COPYALL flag to preserve all file attributes, and schedule copies in nightly windows to reduce impact.
Mount the FSx share on an EC2 instance in a VPN-connected VPC, use rsync over SSH from the on-premises server to the EC2 instance, and copy files from EC2 to the FSx share using Windows file copy.

Export the file server data to AWS Snowball Edge devices, ship to AWS for import to S3, then use DataSync to copy from S3 to FSx for Windows File Server, preserving metadata during the final copy step.

explanation: DataSync natively supports SMB source with full NTFS permission, ACL, and metadata preservation. The on-premises agent handles data transfer efficiently over Direct Connect. DataSync provides incremental transfer for subsequent syncs. This is purpose-built for this migration scenario. Robocopy (B) works but is slower for 50 TB and 500M files without DataSync's optimization. Snowball to S3 (C) loses NTFS permissions during the S3 intermediate step. Rsync over SSH (D) doesn't preserve Windows NTFS permissions.

stem: A company runs a centralized logging platform in a shared services account that receives logs from 300 accounts via Kinesis Data Streams. The logging platform runs on an EKS cluster processing 10 GB of logs per minute. The platform team needs to ensure that log producers in member accounts cannot overwhelm the central logging infrastructure. Which approach provides back-pressure and rate control for log ingestion?

options.text: Implement API Gateway as an ingestion endpoint with per-account usage plans and throttling, forward logs to Kinesis via Lambda, and set rate limits per account based on their expected log volume.
Use Amazon MSK with per-topic quotas for each member account, configure producer quotas to limit throughput per account, and set up consumer lag monitoring on the EKS-based processing cluster.

Configure Kinesis Data Streams with provisioned shard capacity and shard-level metrics, deploy per-account Kinesis producers with rate limiting, and use CloudWatch alarms on WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded.

Deploy Kinesis Data Firehose for each member account instead of Data Streams, configure Firehose buffer sizes and intervals for controlled delivery, and use Firehose delivery stream metrics for monitoring.

explanation: API Gateway usage plans with per-account API keys provide granular rate limiting. Each account gets a throttle limit matching their expected volume. Lambda forwards to Kinesis at a controlled rate. This prevents any single account from overwhelming the system. Kinesis shard-level throttling (A) applies globally, not per-account. Firehose (B) doesn't provide per-producer rate limiting. MSK producer quotas (C) work but require managing Kafka infrastructure and per-account topic configuration is complex at 300 accounts.

stem: A company is building a platform for running scientific simulations that require thousands of GPUs for several hours per simulation. Simulations run 2-3 times per week and the company wants to minimize costs. The simulation framework uses MPI for inter-node communication requiring high-bandwidth, low-latency networking. Which architecture optimizes GPU costs for periodic simulations?

options.text: Deploy EKS with GPU node pools using P5 instances, configure Karpenter for scaling to zero between simulations, use the MPI Operator for job scheduling, and request Spot Instances for GPU nodes.
Deploy Amazon SageMaker training jobs with ml.p5.48xlarge instances, use SageMaker distributed training libraries for MPI communication, submit jobs on-demand, and pay only for training job duration.

Use AWS ParallelCluster with Slurm scheduler, configure P5 instances with EFA in placement groups, enable auto-scaling to zero between simulations, and use On-Demand Capacity Reservations for guaranteed access.

Use EC2 P5 instances in a cluster placement group with EFA enabled for MPI communication, request capacity through EC2 Capacity Reservations on simulation days, and use Spot Instances for cost savings.

explanation: ParallelCluster with Slurm is purpose-built for HPC workloads. Auto-scaling to zero eliminates costs between the 2-3 weekly simulations. EFA in placement groups provides the high-bandwidth, low-latency MPI networking required. On-Demand Capacity Reservations guarantee GPU availability. EC2 with Spot (A) risks interruption during multi-hour simulations. SageMaker training (B) doesn't provide the MPI networking control needed for scientific simulations. EKS with Spot GPUs (D) risks interruption and adds Kubernetes management overhead.

stem: A company's Lambda functions process events from multiple SQS queues. The functions use the same code but different environment variables per queue. The team manages 40 separate Lambda function deployments, each with its own CloudFormation stack. Updating the shared code requires deploying to all 40 functions. Which approach simplifies code management while maintaining per-queue configuration?

options.text: Consolidate to a single Lambda function with event source mappings for all 40 queues, use the event source ARN in the code to determine queue-specific behavior, and store per-queue config in Parameter Store.

Use a single Lambda function with SQS as a trigger, deploy 40 versions with aliases pointing to different configurations, configure each SQS queue to invoke the function via its specific alias endpoint.

Create a Lambda Layer containing the shared business logic, deploy the layer version across all 40 functions, update only the layer when shared code changes, and keep per-function environment variables.

Replace all 40 Lambda functions with a single ECS Fargate service that polls all 40 SQS queues, implement queue-specific processing logic in a configuration file, and deploy as a single container image.

explanation: A single Lambda function with multiple SQS event source mappings eliminates 39 redundant deployments. The event source ARN in the event payload identifies which queue triggered the invocation. Parameter Store provides per-queue configuration without environment variables. Code updates deploy once. Lambda Layers (B) still require maintaining 40 function deployments. Lambda versions with aliases (C) don't support different environment variables per alias. ECS Fargate (D) adds infrastructure management and isn't serverless.

stem: A company wants to implement network segmentation across 50 VPCs connected via Transit Gateway. The company requires that production VPCs cannot communicate with development VPCs, shared services VPCs can reach all VPCs, and VPCs within the same environment can communicate freely. Which Transit Gateway configuration implements this segmentation?

options.text: Use security groups and NACLs on each VPC to block traffic from non-allowed CIDR ranges, maintain a single Transit Gateway route table with all VPC routes, and update security rules when VPCs are added.

Deploy separate Transit Gateways for production and development environments, create Transit Gateway peering between each and a shared services Transit Gateway, and route traffic through peering attachments.

Configure Transit Gateway with a single route table, use VPC prefix lists to control routing, implement AWS Network Firewall between segments for traffic filtering, and create firewall rules per environment.

Create Transit Gateway route tables for production, development, and shared services segments, associate VPCs with their segment route table, propagate routes from shared services to all tables and within-segment only.

explanation: Transit Gateway route table segmentation provides native network isolation. Production route table has routes only to production VPCs and shared services. Development route table has routes only to development VPCs and shared services. Shared services route table has routes to all VPCs. This is the standard TGW segmentation pattern. Security groups/NACLs (B) don't scale and are error-prone across 50 VPCs. Separate Transit Gateways (C) add cost and complexity unnecessarily. Network Firewall (D) adds latency and cost for what route tables solve natively.

stem: A company is building a customer identity and access management (CIAM) platform for their consumer-facing application with 10 million users. The platform must support social login (Google, Facebook, Apple), multi-factor authentication, and custom sign-up flows with email verification. User profiles must be extensible with custom attributes. Which architecture provides enterprise-grade CIAM capabilities?

options.text: Use Amazon Cognito User Pools with social identity provider federation for Google, Facebook, and Apple, configure MFA with TOTP and SMS, use Lambda triggers for custom sign-up flows, and store custom attributes.

Deploy a custom authentication system using API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB for user storage, implement OAuth 2.0 flows manually, integrate social providers via their SDKs, and build custom MFA logic.

Use IAM Identity Center with external identity provider integration for social logins, configure MFA policies, and store user profiles in a DynamoDB table linked to Identity Center user IDs for custom attributes.

Deploy Keycloak on ECS Fargate as an open-source identity provider, configure social login federation, enable built-in MFA support, use Keycloak's custom themes for sign-up flows, and store profiles in RDS.

explanation: Cognito User Pools is purpose-built for CIAM with native social provider federation, MFA (TOTP, SMS, email), Lambda triggers for custom workflows, and custom attributes supporting 10M+ users. Hosted UI provides ready-made sign-up/sign-in flows. Custom authentication (B) requires building and maintaining a complete identity platform. IAM Identity Center (C) is for workforce identity, not consumer CIAM. Keycloak on ECS (D) requires managing infrastructure, scaling, and patching for a managed service alternative.

stem: A company is modernizing its reporting system that generates complex PDF reports by querying a relational database and formatting results with Crystal Reports. The system generates 500 reports daily, each taking 2-10 minutes. The Crystal Reports server runs on Windows and requires a GUI session. Which modernization approach replaces the Crystal Reports dependency?

options.text: Use Amazon QuickSight for all reporting needs, convert Crystal Reports layouts to QuickSight dashboards, schedule dashboard PDF exports via the QuickSight API, and distribute via email subscriptions.

Deploy JasperReports Server on ECS containers as an open-source Crystal Reports replacement, convert report templates to JRXML format, connect to Aurora for data, and schedule via cron in the container.

Rehost Crystal Reports Server on EC2 Windows instances with RDP access, connect to RDS for data, auto-scale instance count based on report queue depth, and store generated PDFs in S3 for distribution.

Use AWS Lambda with a headless Chromium layer to render HTML reports to PDF, query Aurora for data, use S3 for template storage and PDF output, and schedule via EventBridge Scheduler for daily generation.

explanation: Lambda with headless Chromium generates PDFs from HTML templates serverlessly. Aurora provides the relational database. S3 stores templates and outputs. EventBridge schedules daily generation. This eliminates Windows/GUI dependencies and scales automatically. Rehosting Crystal Reports (B) doesn't modernize—it moves the same dependency to cloud. QuickSight (C) doesn't support the complex formatting of Crystal Reports layouts. JasperReports on ECS (D) replaces one reporting server with another, still requiring infrastructure management.

stem: A company's DynamoDB table has a hot partition problem. The table has a composite primary key with tenant_id as partition key and timestamp as sort key. One tenant generates 80% of all writes, causing ProvisionedThroughputExceededException for that partition while other partitions are underutilized. Which approach resolves the hot partition without changing the data model significantly?

options.text: Add a random suffix (0-9) to the tenant_id partition key for the high-volume tenant, creating 10 logical partitions, and implement scatter-gather reads that query all 10 partitions and merge results client-side.
Increase the provisioned write capacity units to 10x the current value to ensure the hot partition has enough capacity, and monitor with CloudWatch alarms to scale capacity further if needed.
Enable DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for write-through caching, which absorbs write spikes in the DAX cache layer before writing to DynamoDB, reducing the write pressure on the hot partition.

Switch the table to on-demand capacity mode which automatically handles hot partitions by distributing traffic across more physical partitions, and remove provisioned throughput configuration entirely.

explanation: Write sharding with a random suffix distributes the hot tenant's writes across 10 physical partitions, each handling 10% of the traffic. Scatter-gather reads query all suffixed partitions. This directly addresses the hot partition problem. On-demand mode (B) adapts to overall table traffic but doesn't solve single-partition throughput limits—each partition still has a per-partition limit. DAX (C) caches reads, not writes. Increasing total WCUs (D) doesn't help because the limit is per-partition, not table-wide.

stem: A company uses multiple AWS accounts for different business units. Each business unit has its own VPC with overlapping CIDR ranges (all use 10.0.0.0/16). The company now needs these VPCs to communicate for a cross-business-unit application. Re-addressing the VPCs is not feasible. Which approach enables communication between VPCs with overlapping CIDRs?

options.text: Implement a hub-and-spoke network using a shared VPC with unique CIDRs, deploy NAT instances in the hub VPC to translate between overlapping ranges, and route all inter-VPC traffic through the hub.
Deploy Transit Gateway and attach all VPCs, configure Transit Gateway route tables with routes for each VPC CIDR, and use Transit Gateway prefix lists to differentiate between the overlapping ranges.

Deploy AWS PrivateLink with NLB in each VPC to expose services as VPC endpoint services, create interface VPC endpoints in consuming VPCs, routing traffic through PrivateLink without requiring unique CIDRs.

Create VPC peering connections between all VPCs, configure route tables with more specific routes to direct traffic to the correct peer, and use security groups to control access between business units.

explanation: PrivateLink enables service-to-service communication without requiring unique CIDRs. Each service is exposed through an NLB and consumed via interface endpoints. Traffic stays on the AWS network and CIDR overlap is irrelevant. VPC peering (B) does not work with overlapping CIDRs—it's a hard requirement for unique ranges. Transit Gateway (C) also cannot route between overlapping CIDRs. NAT instances for translation (D) add complexity, latency, and become single points of failure.

stem: A company is designing a disaster recovery solution for a critical application with an RPO of 1 minute and RTO of 5 minutes. The application uses Aurora MySQL, ElastiCache for Redis, and ECS Fargate services. Which TWO components are required to meet these DR objectives? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure Aurora Global Database with a secondary Region for sub-second RPO and sub-minute RTO on database failover, enable write forwarding during normal operation for read scalability in the DR Region.

Deploy ElastiCache Global Datastore for Redis with automatic failover to replicate cache data to the DR Region, ensuring cached session data and application state survive a regional outage completely.

Deploy ECS Fargate services in the DR Region in a scaled-down configuration with Route 53 health checks for automatic DNS failover, pre-pull container images to ECR in the DR Region for faster startup.
Take Aurora automated backups every hour and copy to the DR Region using cross-region backup, restore from the most recent backup during failover, and reconnect ECS services to the restored database.

explanation: Aurora Global Database provides RPO under 1 second and RTO under 1 minute with managed failover. ElastiCache Global Datastore replicates Redis data cross-region for cache continuity during failover. Both provide the sub-minute RPO and rapid RTO needed. Hourly backups (C) give at best 1-hour RPO, violating the 1-minute requirement. ECS Fargate with Route 53 (D) helps with RTO but isn't sufficient alone—the data layer (Aurora and Redis) is the critical RPO component.

stem: A company has an on-premises ETL pipeline built with Informatica PowerCenter that processes data from 50 source systems. The pipeline runs 200 ETL jobs nightly with complex transformations including data quality rules, SCD Type 2 handling, and data lineage tracking. Which AWS service replaces Informatica PowerCenter with equivalent capabilities?

options.text: Use AWS Glue Studio with visual ETL designer for transformation logic, Glue Data Quality for data validation rules, Glue Data Catalog for lineage tracking, and Glue workflows for job orchestration and scheduling.

Deploy Apache Airflow on Amazon MWAA for job orchestration, write ETL transformations in PySpark on EMR, implement data quality checks in Great Expectations, and track lineage in a custom metadata store.

Use Amazon Redshift stored procedures for all ETL transformations, implement SCD Type 2 using Redshift MERGE statements, use Redshift system tables for lineage, and schedule via Redshift query scheduler.

Deploy Informatica Cloud on EC2 instances as a lift-and-shift, connect to S3 and Redshift as targets, maintain existing PowerCenter mappings and workflows, and use existing Informatica licenses on AWS.

explanation: Glue Studio provides visual ETL design similar to Informatica's mapping designer. Glue Data Quality validates data against rules. Data Catalog tracks schema and lineage. Glue workflows orchestrate the 200 jobs with dependencies. This is a managed replacement for PowerCenter. MWAA with EMR/Spark (B) requires building the ETL framework from scratch. Redshift stored procedures (C) are limited for complex ETL orchestration. Informatica on EC2 (D) doesn't modernize—it replicates the on-premises setup.

stem: A company's EC2 Auto Scaling group launches instances that take 5 minutes to become healthy due to application startup, dependency checks, and cache warming. During scale-out events, the ALB sends traffic to new instances before they are ready, causing HTTP 503 errors. Which approach prevents traffic from reaching instances before they are fully healthy?

options.text: Add an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook on the EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING transition, run initialization scripts via SSM Run Command, send CONTINUE after initialization completes, then register with the target group.

Configure ALB target group health checks with a custom health check path that returns 200 only after full initialization, set health check interval to 10 seconds, and set the healthy threshold to 3 consecutive checks.

Increase the ALB deregistration delay to 300 seconds to keep old instances receiving traffic longer, giving new instances time to warm up before old instances are fully deregistered from the target group.
Configure the Auto Scaling group's default instance warmup to 300 seconds which prevents the group from scaling based on metrics from newly launched instances, and set a minimum healthy percentage.

explanation: Lifecycle hooks pause the instance in a Pending:Wait state during launch. SSM Run Command executes initialization, dependency checks, and cache warming. The instance only enters InService (and gets registered with ALB) after CONTINUE is sent. This ensures full readiness before receiving traffic. ALB health checks (A) still register the instance—it receives traffic during the 5-minute startup even if health checks fail, causing 503s until the instance is deregistered. Deregistration delay (C) affects termination, not launch. Default warmup (D) affects scaling decisions, not traffic routing.

stem: A company acquired a startup that operates entirely in a single AWS account with no organizational structure. The startup's account contains production workloads, developer sandboxes, and shared infrastructure in a single VPC. The company needs to integrate the startup into their existing AWS Organization while separating workloads. Which approach safely integrates the acquired account?

options.text: Invite the startup's account into the Organization under a sandbox OU with restrictive SCPs, gradually create new accounts for production workloads, migrate production first, then development, then decommission.

Invite the startup's account into the Organization, create new accounts for production and development, use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate workloads to the appropriate new accounts, and decommission resources.

Create new VPCs in the startup's account for production and development, use VPC peering between them, move resources between VPCs using CloudFormation, and invite the account into the Organization afterward.

Create a new AWS account in the Organization for the startup, export all AMIs and data from the original account, import into the new account, recreate all resources using CloudFormation, and close the original account.

explanation: Adding the account to a sandbox OU with restrictive SCPs immediately applies security guardrails while keeping production running. New accounts in proper OUs receive full governance. Migrating production first minimizes risk exposure. Gradual migration prevents disruption. Creating new accounts and migrating with MGN (A) requires migrating before applying governance. VPC reorganization within one account (B) doesn't achieve account-level separation. Recreating everything in a new account (C) is error-prone and risks data loss.

stem: A company is designing an IoT fleet management platform for 1 million connected vehicles. Each vehicle sends GPS coordinates, engine diagnostics, and driver behavior data every second. The platform must detect maintenance alerts in real-time, store raw telemetry for 90 days, and provide historical analytics. Which architecture handles this data volume and variety?

options.text: Deploy Amazon MSK for high-throughput message ingestion from vehicles over Kafka protocol, process with Spark Streaming on EMR for alerts, store in HDFS on EMR for 90 days, and query with Presto on EMR.

Use IoT Core for connectivity, store all telemetry in DynamoDB with auto-scaling for real-time queries, implement alert detection in Lambda triggered by DynamoDB Streams, and export to S3 for historical analytics.

Use IoT Core for device connectivity with MQTT, IoT Rules Engine to route to Kinesis Data Streams for real-time processing, Managed Flink for alert detection, Firehose to S3 for storage, and Athena for analytics.

Use API Gateway WebSocket APIs for vehicle connectivity, SQS for message queuing, Lambda for real-time alert processing, store data directly in DynamoDB with TTL for 90-day retention, and Redshift for analytics.

explanation: IoT Core handles 1M devices with MQTT at scale. Kinesis ingests 1M events/second. Managed Flink provides real-time alert detection with complex event processing. Firehose delivers to S3 for cost-effective 90-day storage. Athena provides serverless analytics on S3. This is fully managed and scales. API Gateway WebSocket (B) isn't designed for IoT scale and SQS adds latency. DynamoDB for all telemetry (C) is cost-prohibitive at 1M events/second for 90 days. EMR/MSK (D) requires managing cluster infrastructure.

stem: A company's application uses CloudFront to serve static assets. Cache hit ratio is only 40% despite assets being cacheable. Investigation reveals that query string parameters vary across requests for the same content (tracking parameters, session IDs). The assets themselves are identical regardless of these parameters. Which optimization improves the cache hit ratio?

options.text: Increase the CloudFront cache TTL to 30 days for all static assets, configure custom error pages for cache misses, and enable Origin Shield to improve cache fill ratios from the origin server.

Enable CloudFront real-time logs to analyze cache misses, configure Lambda@Edge to strip query strings from the origin request, and add Cache-Control headers with long max-age at the origin S3 bucket.

Configure the CloudFront cache policy to ignore all query strings for static asset behaviors, or forward only the query strings that determine content variation, maximizing cache hits for identical content.

Migrate static assets from S3 to a dedicated CloudFront origin group with multiple origins for redundancy, enable field-level encryption for tracking parameters, and configure S3 versioning for cache busting.

explanation: Query string variations create different cache keys for identical content. Configuring the cache policy to ignore irrelevant query strings (tracking, session) means CloudFront treats all requests for the same path as one cache entry. This directly increases cache hit ratio from 40% to near 100% for static assets. Increasing TTL (B) doesn't help when every request creates a unique cache key. Lambda@Edge stripping (C) works but is more complex and costly than cache policy configuration. Origin groups (D) address availability, not cache hit ratio.

stem: A company has a monolithic .NET application running on IIS with a SQL Server backend. The application uses Windows-specific features including COM interop, Windows Services, and MSMQ for asynchronous messaging. The company wants to modernize incrementally. Which first step creates the greatest modernization value with the least risk?

options.text: Extract the MSMQ message handlers into separate Lambda functions, migrate SQL Server to RDS, move the IIS application to Elastic Beanstalk, and replace COM interop with REST API calls to microservices.
Migrate MSMQ to Amazon SQS by replacing the MSMQ client code with the AWS SDK SQS client, keeping the rest of the application unchanged on IIS, and decommissioning the MSMQ service on the server.

Rewrite the entire application in .NET 8 on Linux, replace all Windows-specific features with cross-platform alternatives, deploy on ECS Fargate with Linux containers, and migrate SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL.

Containerize the application using Windows containers with App2Container, deploy on ECS with Windows nodes, maintain all Windows dependencies including COM interop and MSMQ inside the container image.

explanation: Replacing MSMQ with SQS is a targeted change that removes a Windows dependency while providing a managed, scalable messaging service. The SQS client API maps well to MSMQ patterns. The rest of the application remains unchanged, minimizing risk. Full rewrite to .NET 8 (B) is the highest risk approach for a first step. Containerizing unchanged (C) preserves all dependencies without modernization. Extracting to Lambda and Beanstalk (D) changes too many components simultaneously for an incremental first step.

stem: A company needs to centrally manage TLS certificates for 500 applications across 80 accounts. Certificates must be automatically renewed before expiration, and the security team must be notified 30 days before any certificate expires. The company uses both ALBs and CloudFront distributions. Which approach provides centralized certificate lifecycle management?

options.text: Use AWS Certificate Manager in each account with DNS validation via Route 53 for automatic renewal, configure ACM expiration EventBridge events forwarded to a central account, and trigger SNS notifications 30 days before.

Use AWS Private CA for all certificates, deploy a central CA hierarchy in the security account, share via RAM to all accounts, configure CRL distribution, and monitor certificate expiration via CA audit reports.

Purchase certificates from a third-party CA, upload to IAM certificate store in each account, create Lambda functions to check expiration dates daily, and send SNS notifications when certificates approach expiration.

Create a single ACM certificate with 500 SANs (Subject Alternative Names) in the management account, share the certificate to all accounts via RAM, and configure automatic renewal with DNS validation.

explanation: ACM with DNS validation provides fully automatic renewal for certificates on ALBs and CloudFront. EventBridge captures ACM expiration events and forwards to a central monitoring account. SNS notifications alert the security team 30 days before expiration as a safety net. Third-party certificates (B) don't auto-renew and require manual management. Private CA (C) is for internal certificates, not public-facing TLS. A single certificate with 500 SANs (D) isn't practical—ACM has SAN limits and cannot be shared via RAM.

stem: A company is designing a platform for processing insurance claims. Each claim goes through a multi-step workflow: document intake, OCR processing, fraud screening, adjuster review, payment calculation, and disbursement. Some steps require human approval, and the workflow may take days to complete. Which architecture supports long-running workflows with human-in-the-loop steps?

options.text: Use Step Functions Standard Workflows with task tokens for human approval steps, integrate with SES for email notifications to adjusters, use callbacks from a web application to resume the workflow after approval.

Use Step Functions Express Workflows for fast claim processing, implement human approval as Lambda functions polling DynamoDB for approval status, and set Lambda timeout to maximum 15 minutes per approval check.

Build a custom workflow engine using DynamoDB for state tracking, SQS for step transitions, Lambda for processing each step, and a web application for human approval that updates DynamoDB to advance the claim.

Use Amazon SWF (Simple Workflow Service) for long-running workflow orchestration, implement activity workers on EC2 for each processing step, and use SWF decision tasks for routing claims through the workflow.

explanation: Step Functions Standard Workflows support executions up to 1 year, ideal for multi-day claim processing. Task tokens pause execution until an external callback resumes it, perfect for human-in-the-loop approval. SES notifies adjusters. Web callback with the task token resumes processing. Express Workflows (B) have a 5-minute maximum duration, insufficient for multi-day workflows. Custom DynamoDB workflow (C) requires building state machine logic from scratch. SWF (D) is a legacy service superseded by Step Functions.

stem: A company's application uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with Multi-AZ deployment. During a planned maintenance window, the failover to the standby takes 60-90 seconds, causing application errors because the database connection strings use the instance endpoint rather than the cluster endpoint. Connection pools don't automatically reconnect. Which improvement reduces failover impact?

options.text: Upgrade to a larger RDS instance class to reduce maintenance frequency, schedule maintenance during periods of zero traffic, and pre-scale the application before maintenance windows to handle connection storms.

Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL which provides faster failover (under 30 seconds), use the Aurora cluster endpoint, and configure application connection pools with shorter TCP keepalive timers and reconnection logic.

Switch to the RDS cluster endpoint, deploy RDS Proxy for connection pooling with automatic failover handling, configure the application to use the RDS Proxy endpoint, and enable RDS Proxy multiplexing.

Add read replicas and distribute read traffic across them, use the instance endpoint for writes only, implement application-level retry logic with exponential backoff, and configure shorter connection timeouts.

explanation: RDS Proxy maintains a connection pool that handles failover transparently. Applications connect to the proxy endpoint, which automatically redirects to the new primary after failover. This eliminates application-level connection management issues. The cluster endpoint ensures the correct instance is targeted. Aurora migration (B) improves failover time but still requires connection handling changes. Read replicas (C) don't help with write-path failover. Larger instances and scheduling (D) don't address the core failover handling problem.

stem: A company is migrating a large SAN (Storage Area Network) with 200 TB of block storage used by VMware virtual machines. The SAN provides iSCSI volumes to 50 VMs. The company wants to maintain block storage access patterns during migration while minimizing data transfer time. Which approach migrates SAN storage efficiently?

options.text: Export SAN LUNs as VMDK files, upload to S3 using S3 Transfer Acceleration, import VMDKs as AMIs using VM Import/Export, launch EC2 instances from the imported AMIs, and attach additional EBS volumes.

Deploy AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in cached mode on-premises, present iSCSI volumes to VMs, migrate data to AWS asynchronously, then migrate VMs to EC2 with EBS volumes created from gateway snapshots.

Use AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices to copy SAN data, ship to AWS for import to S3, convert S3 objects to EBS snapshots, create EBS volumes from snapshots, and attach to migrated EC2 instances.

Use AWS Application Migration Service to replicate each VM's storage to AWS via Direct Connect, which automatically replicates block-level data to EBS volumes in the target Region for each migrated server.

explanation: Application Migration Service (MGN) performs continuous block-level replication of VM disks to EBS volumes. Each VM's storage is replicated over Direct Connect with minimal downtime at cutover. This handles all 50 VMs and their block storage without intermediate steps. Storage Gateway (A) adds an intermediate caching layer that slows migration. Snowball (B) involves physical shipping time and complex conversion steps. VMDK export/import (C) requires extended downtime during export and upload of 200 TB.

stem: A company needs to establish a central network inspection architecture where all internet-bound traffic from 100 VPCs passes through a centralized firewall for deep packet inspection and IDS/IPS. The firewall must inspect both inbound and outbound traffic. Which network architecture centralizes traffic inspection?

options.text: Use AWS WAF on all ALBs across 100 VPCs for web traffic inspection, configure WAF rules for IDS/IPS equivalent functionality, use Security Groups as the primary network-level filtering mechanism for all traffic.

Deploy AWS Network Firewall in an inspection VPC, route all traffic through Transit Gateway to the inspection VPC, configure TGW route tables to direct internet-bound traffic through the firewall, and NAT Gateway for egress.

Configure VPC Flow Logs for all 100 VPCs, stream logs to a central SIEM for analysis, detect threats using GuardDuty, and manually block malicious IPs using NACLs after threat detection and investigation.

Deploy third-party firewall appliances on EC2 in each of the 100 VPCs, manage firewall rules centrally via the vendor's management console, and configure each VPC's route table to route through the local firewall.

explanation: Network Firewall in a centralized inspection VPC provides stateful deep packet inspection, IDS/IPS, and TLS inspection. Transit Gateway routes all internet-bound traffic through the inspection VPC. This provides single-pane inspection for all 100 VPCs. Firewalls in each VPC (B) creates 100 firewall deployments to manage. WAF (C) only inspects HTTP/HTTPS, not all traffic, and doesn't provide IDS/IPS. Flow Logs with GuardDuty (D) is detective, not preventive—threats are detected after the fact.

stem: A company is designing a data mesh architecture where each business domain owns its data products. Each domain team publishes curated datasets that other teams can discover and consume. The platform must provide data cataloging, access control, and cross-account data sharing. Which architecture enables a data mesh on AWS?

options.text: Deploy each domain's data in separate Glue Data Catalogs, use S3 Access Points for cross-account access, implement IAM policies for fine-grained permissions, and build a custom discovery portal with API Gateway.

Create a central data warehouse in Redshift where all domains load their data, use Redshift data sharing for cross-team access, implement column-level security with Redshift views, and use Redshift catalog for discovery.

Use AWS Lake Formation with data mesh blueprints, configure per-domain data catalogs with Lake Formation permissions, enable cross-account data sharing via Lake Formation tags, and use DataZone for data discovery.
Deploy Apache Atlas on EMR for data cataloging, use Apache Ranger for access control, share data via S3 bucket policies between accounts, and build a custom data marketplace portal for domain teams.

explanation: Lake Formation provides centralized governance with decentralized ownership—each domain manages its data with Lake Formation tag-based access control. Cross-account sharing is native. DataZone provides a business data catalog for discovery and self-service access requests. This matches data mesh principles. Apache Atlas/Ranger (B) requires managing open-source infrastructure. Central Redshift (C) creates a data monolith, opposite of data mesh. Custom Glue catalogs with S3 Access Points (D) requires building governance and discovery from scratch.

stem: A company's containerized application on EKS uses persistent volumes backed by EBS gp2 volumes. Database containers experience I/O bottlenecks during peak hours with IOPS exceeding the gp2 baseline of 3,000. The team has over-provisioned volume sizes to get more baseline IOPS (3 IOPS per GB), wasting 70% of storage capacity. Which optimization reduces costs while meeting IOPS requirements?

options.text: Migrate persistent volumes from gp2 to gp3 volume type which provides 3,000 baseline IOPS regardless of size, configure additional provisioned IOPS as needed, and right-size the volumes to actual capacity needs.

Implement EBS volume striping by creating RAID 0 arrays from multiple smaller gp2 volumes attached to each node, aggregating IOPS across volumes, and managing the RAID configuration in the container runtime.

Replace EBS gp2 volumes with io2 Block Express volumes for maximum IOPS performance, configure provisioned IOPS at the required level, and right-size volumes to actual capacity without IOPS considerations.
Migrate database workloads from EBS-backed persistent volumes to Amazon FSx for Lustre for high-performance storage, configure Lustre with SSD storage tier, and mount via CSI driver in EKS.

explanation: gp3 decouples IOPS from volume size—3,000 IOPS baseline at any size. Volumes can be right-sized to actual capacity (reducing 70% waste) while maintaining or exceeding IOPS requirements. Additional IOPS can be provisioned independently up to 16,000. gp3 is also 20% cheaper per GB than gp2. FSx for Lustre (B) is overkill for database I/O—it's designed for HPC workloads. io2 Block Express (C) is significantly more expensive than gp3 for this use case. RAID 0 striping (D) adds operational complexity and reduces reliability.

stem: A company runs a real-time data warehouse on Teradata with 500 TB of data. The Teradata system uses proprietary SQL extensions, BTEQ scripts for loading, and FastLoad/MultiLoad utilities. The company needs to migrate to AWS while preserving the investment in existing SQL queries and ETL logic. Which migration approach minimizes query rewriting?

options.text: Migrate data to Amazon Redshift using DMS, manually rewrite all Teradata SQL extensions to standard ANSI SQL, replace BTEQ with psql client, and implement custom loading pipelines using AWS Glue ETL jobs.

Use AWS Schema Conversion Tool to assess and convert Teradata SQL to Amazon Redshift SQL, migrate data with DMS, convert BTEQ scripts to Redshift RSQL, and replace FastLoad with COPY from S3 with Redshift.
Load Teradata data into Amazon S3 as Parquet files, query with Athena using standard SQL, rewrite all Teradata-specific SQL to Athena Presto SQL, and replace all ETL scripts with Glue PySpark jobs.

Deploy Teradata Vantage on EC2 instances as a cloud lift-and-shift, maintain all existing SQL and utilities unchanged, configure Direct Connect for hybrid queries, and gradually migrate queries to Redshift.

explanation: SCT automates Teradata-to-Redshift SQL conversion, minimizing manual rewriting. DMS handles data migration. RSQL replaces BTEQ with similar syntax. COPY command replaces FastLoad for bulk loading. Redshift's SQL compatibility with Teradata reduces conversion effort. Manual rewriting to ANSI SQL (B) is time-consuming for 500 TB of queries. Athena/Presto (C) requires different SQL dialects and doesn't match Teradata's real-time analytics capability. Teradata on EC2 (D) doesn't modernize and maintains expensive licensing.

stem: A company needs to manage DNS across 200 accounts where each account hosts applications with their own subdomains under the company's apex domain. Currently each team manages Route 53 hosted zones independently, causing conflicting records and no centralized oversight. Which approach centralizes DNS management while allowing team autonomy for their subdomains?

options.text: Consolidate all DNS records into a single Route 53 hosted zone in the management account, grant IAM cross-account access for teams to manage their records, and use resource record-level IAM policies for isolation.
Use AWS Cloud Map for all service DNS registration across accounts, configure Cloud Map to automatically create Route 53 records, and manage namespace-level permissions for each team's services.

Deploy a BIND DNS server on EC2 in a central account as the authoritative nameserver, configure all accounts to use the BIND server via Route 53 Resolver rules, and manage zones centrally on the BIND server.

Create a central Route 53 hosted zone for the apex domain in a networking account, delegate subdomains to hosted zones in each application account using NS records, and use SCPs to protect the central zone.

explanation: Central hosted zone for the apex domain provides oversight and control. NS delegation to account-specific hosted zones gives each team full control over their subdomain records. SCPs protect the central zone from unauthorized modifications. This is the standard DNS delegation pattern. Single consolidated zone (B) creates a management bottleneck and risk—IAM policies can't provide subdomain-level isolation for Route 53 records. BIND on EC2 (C) requires managing DNS infrastructure. Cloud Map (D) is for service discovery, not general DNS management.

stem: A company is designing a compliance monitoring platform that must continuously evaluate 200 security controls across 500 accounts, generate compliance scores per account and control, and produce audit-ready evidence packages for SOC 2 and PCI DSS frameworks. Which architecture provides continuous compliance monitoring with audit evidence?

options.text: Use Security Hub with CIS and PCI DSS standards enabled across all accounts, aggregate findings to a central security account, export findings to S3, and generate compliance reports using Athena queries.

Build a custom compliance platform using Lambda functions that query AWS Config, CloudTrail, and IAM across all accounts, calculate compliance scores in DynamoDB, and generate PDF reports using QuickSight.

Deploy AWS Config conformance packs for SOC 2 and PCI DSS across all accounts via StackSets, aggregate results in a central account, build QuickSight dashboards for compliance scores, and manually collect evidence.
Use AWS Audit Manager with SOC 2 and PCI DSS pre-built frameworks, configure automated evidence collection from AWS Config, CloudTrail, and Security Hub, and generate assessment reports for auditors.

explanation: Audit Manager provides pre-built SOC 2 and PCI DSS frameworks with automated evidence collection. It integrates with Config, CloudTrail, and Security Hub for continuous assessment. Evidence is organized into audit-ready packages with assessment reports. This is purpose-built for compliance audits. Config conformance packs (B) evaluate rules but don't produce audit evidence packages. Security Hub (C) focuses on security findings, not structured audit evidence. Custom Lambda platform (D) requires building the entire compliance framework from scratch.

stem: A company's VPN connection between their on-premises data center and AWS VPC has a maximum throughput of 1.25 Gbps. The company needs 5 Gbps of bandwidth for data replication to AWS. Setting up a new Direct Connect connection will take 3 months. Which approach increases bandwidth immediately while waiting for Direct Connect?

options.text: Upgrade the VPN connection to use a larger virtual private gateway that supports higher throughput, configure jumbo frames on the VPN tunnels, and enable VPN acceleration for improved performance.

Create multiple Site-to-Site VPN connections over the existing internet link, configure ECMP (Equal-Cost Multi-Path) routing on Transit Gateway to aggregate bandwidth across VPN tunnels up to 50 Gbps.

Set up AWS VPN CloudHub by creating multiple VPN connections to different virtual private gateways in different VPCs, distribute traffic across the VPN connections using Route 53 weighted routing policies.
Deploy a software VPN appliance on EC2 with enhanced networking, create a GRE tunnel over the internet to the on-premises router, and use the EC2 instance's network bandwidth for higher throughput.

explanation: Transit Gateway supports ECMP across multiple VPN connections. Each VPN connection provides up to 1.25 Gbps. Four connections with ECMP achieve 5 Gbps aggregate bandwidth immediately using the existing internet connection. This is a native AWS solution. Upgrading VPN (B) isn't possible—1.25 Gbps is the per-connection limit. CloudHub (C) is for branch-to-branch connectivity, not bandwidth aggregation. Software VPN on EC2 (D) adds complexity and the instance becomes a bandwidth bottleneck.

stem: A company is modernizing its on-premises Elasticsearch cluster (version 5.6) used for application log analytics and full-text search. The cluster has 30 TB of data with 100 indexes. The company wants to upgrade to the latest version and move to a managed service. Elasticsearch 5.6 uses deprecated mapping types that are incompatible with newer versions. Which migration approach handles the version incompatibility?

options.text: Export all data from Elasticsearch 5.6 to JSON files using elasticdump, upload to S3, modify index mappings to remove deprecated types, and bulk import into a new OpenSearch Service cluster on the latest version.
Deploy a new OpenSearch Service cluster on the latest version, use Logstash to reindex data from the old ES 5.6 cluster to the new cluster with mapping type removal transformations during ingestion.

Use the Amazon OpenSearch Service upgrade path: deploy OpenSearch version compatible with ES 5.6, migrate data using snapshot/restore, then perform in-place upgrades through each major version until reaching the latest.

Use AWS DMS to replicate data from Elasticsearch 5.6 to a new OpenSearch Service cluster, configure DMS transformation rules to handle mapping type changes, and perform continuous replication until cutover.

explanation: Logstash can read from ES 5.6 and write to the latest OpenSearch version with transformation pipelines that remove deprecated mapping types during reindex. This handles the version incompatibility in a single migration step. In-place upgrades (A) through every major version is slow and complex for 30 TB across multiple version hops. JSON export with elasticdump (C) is slow for 30 TB and requires manual mapping modification. DMS (D) doesn't support Elasticsearch as a source for full cluster migration.

stem: A company's development teams frequently need temporary elevated permissions to debug production issues. Currently they submit tickets to the security team who manually grants permissions, taking 30 minutes on average. The company needs an automated just-in-time (JIT) access system with approval workflows and automatic expiration. Which architecture implements automated JIT privileged access?

options.text: Create elevated IAM roles in each account, build a Slack-integrated chatbot using Lambda that assumes the elevated role on behalf of developers after receiving emoji approval reactions from managers.

Configure AWS SSO with always-on administrator permission sets, train developers to only use elevated permissions when needed, and rely on CloudTrail for post-hoc auditing of any misuse of elevated access.

Pre-create IAM users with elevated permissions that are disabled by default, build a portal using API Gateway and Lambda that enables the IAM user for 1 hour after ticket approval, then disables automatically.

Use IAM Identity Center with Permission Sets that grant elevated access, implement an approval workflow via Step Functions with SNS notifications for manager approval, and set session duration to 1 hour maximum.

explanation: IAM Identity Center Permission Sets with short session durations provide time-limited access. Step Functions orchestrates the approval workflow with manager notification via SNS and automatic expiration. This is a robust, auditable JIT access solution. Slack chatbot (B) lacks audit trail and enterprise governance controls. Pre-created IAM users (C) with permanent credentials are a security risk even when disabled. Always-on admin access (D) violates least-privilege principles and relies entirely on user self-restraint.

stem: A company is building a platform that needs to run untrusted user-submitted code in sandboxed environments. Each code submission must execute in an isolated environment with no network access, limited CPU/memory, and a 30-second timeout. The platform must handle 10,000 concurrent submissions. Which architecture provides secure sandboxed code execution at scale?

options.text: Use AWS Lambda with custom runtimes for each supported language, configure Lambda functions in a VPC with no internet gateway or NAT for network isolation, set 128 MB memory limit and 30-second timeout.

Deploy EKS pods with gVisor runtime class for kernel-level sandboxing, configure resource limits and network policies denying all traffic, use pod security standards for restricted profiles, and set active deadline.

Use Firecracker microVMs on EC2 bare metal instances for hardware-level isolation, configure each microVM with no network interface, CPU and memory limits, and terminate after 30-second execution timeout.

Deploy AWS Fargate tasks with read-only root filesystem, configure task definitions with CPU and memory limits, use awsvpc networking mode with empty security groups for network isolation, and set stop timeout.

explanation: Fargate tasks provide container-level isolation with microVM technology (Firecracker) underneath. Read-only filesystem prevents persistent changes. Empty security groups block all network traffic. CPU/memory limits are enforced at the task level. Fargate handles 10,000 concurrent tasks without managing infrastructure. Lambda (A) doesn't provide true code execution sandboxing—custom runtimes still share the Lambda execution environment. Custom Firecracker on bare metal (C) requires managing VM orchestration infrastructure. EKS with gVisor (D) requires managing cluster infrastructure and node pools.

stem: A company's data pipeline ingests data from 100 sources into an S3 data lake. Each source delivers data on different schedules (hourly, daily, weekly). Downstream Glue ETL jobs frequently fail because they start before upstream data has arrived. The team manually monitors S3 for new data and triggers jobs via cron schedules with large buffer times. Which approach makes pipeline execution event-driven and reliable?

options.text: Deploy Apache Airflow on MWAA with sensors for each S3 source prefix that poll for new data, define DAGs with dependency chains, and trigger downstream processing when all sensors detect data arrival.

Increase buffer times in cron schedules to ensure all upstream data has arrived before downstream jobs start, add data validation checks at the start of each Glue job, and retry failed jobs automatically after 1 hour.

Configure S3 Event Notifications for each source prefix to trigger EventBridge rules, use Step Functions to track data arrivals and start Glue jobs only when all required source data has landed for each processing window.

Use Glue Triggers with crawler conditions that detect new data in each source prefix, chain Glue jobs using trigger dependencies, and configure retry policies for jobs that find empty datasets from late-arriving sources.

explanation: S3 Event Notifications immediately detect data arrivals without polling. EventBridge routes events to Step Functions which tracks multi-source completion. Glue jobs start only when all required data has landed, eliminating timing failures. This is truly event-driven. Glue crawler triggers (B) add latency from crawling and don't support multi-source dependency tracking. Airflow sensors (C) poll S3, adding latency and cost compared to event-driven S3 notifications. Increasing buffer times (D) wastes time and doesn't guarantee data arrival.

stem: A company has a legacy Java EE application using EJBs, JPA with Oracle, and JMS messaging deployed on WebLogic application server. The application uses WebLogic-specific features including WebLogic clustering, T3 protocol, and WebLogic JNDI. The company wants to move to AWS with minimal code changes. Which migration approach preserves WebLogic compatibility?

options.text: Refactor the application to run on Apache Tomcat by removing all EJB dependencies, replace JPA with lightweight ORM, convert JMS to SQS, deploy on Elastic Beanstalk, and migrate Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL.

Rehost WebLogic on EC2 instances using existing Oracle WebLogic licenses (BYOL), configure WebLogic clustering across multiple EC2 instances, use RDS for Oracle for the database, and Amazon MQ for JMS messaging.

Migrate to AWS Lambda by decomposing EJBs into Lambda functions, replace JPA with DynamoDB SDK calls, convert JMS message-driven beans to SQS-triggered Lambda functions, and eliminate the application server.

Containerize the WebLogic application using Oracle's WebLogic Docker images, deploy on EKS with WebLogic Kubernetes Operator, use RDS for Oracle, and replace JMS with Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ messaging.

explanation: Rehosting WebLogic on EC2 with BYOL preserves all WebLogic-specific features (clustering, T3, JNDI) with zero code changes. RDS for Oracle maintains database compatibility. Amazon MQ provides JMS compatibility. This is the lowest-risk approach for a WebLogic application. Refactoring to Tomcat (B) requires removing EJBs—a significant rewrite. WebLogic on EKS (C) works but adds Kubernetes complexity for a lift-and-shift. Lambda decomposition (D) is a complete rewrite, not minimal code changes.

stem: A company needs to implement a detective control that identifies when IAM access keys are older than 90 days across all 300 accounts in their Organization. Non-compliant keys must be automatically disabled, and the key owner must be notified via email to rotate their key. Which approach provides automated key age compliance?

options.text: Create a Lambda function in the management account that uses Organizations ListAccounts and IAM ListAccessKeys across all accounts, disable old keys, and send notification emails via SES based on user contact tags.

Deploy AWS Config rule iam-access-key-rotation in all accounts via organizational Config, configure SSM Automation remediation to disable old keys, and use SNS to notify key owners identified from IAM user tags.

Implement a credential report-based solution: download IAM credential reports from all accounts weekly, parse for keys older than 90 days in a Lambda function, disable non-compliant keys, and email users via SNS.

Use IAM Access Analyzer to identify access keys not used in 90 days across the Organization, generate findings for unused keys, and create EventBridge rules to trigger Lambda for disabling keys and notifying owners.

explanation: Organizational AWS Config with the iam-access-key-rotation rule automatically evaluates key age across all 300 accounts. SSM Automation provides standardized remediation to disable old keys. SNS notifies owners. This is fully automated and scales with the Organization. Cross-account Lambda (B) requires maintaining credentials and permissions for all 300 accounts. IAM Access Analyzer (C) identifies unused keys, not keys based on age—a key used daily but 91 days old would not be flagged. Weekly credential reports (D) have up to 7-day detection lag.

stem: A company is designing a serverless data processing platform that must handle unpredictable traffic patterns ranging from 0 to 50,000 events per second. The platform must transform events, enrich them with reference data, and load into multiple destinations. Cost optimization during zero-traffic periods is essential. Which TWO components provide cost-effective serverless event processing? (Choose two.)

options.text: Deploy Amazon MSK Serverless for event ingestion which scales automatically and charges only for data processed, providing Kafka-compatible APIs without cluster management or idle capacity costs.

Use Kinesis Data Firehose for all event processing including transformation via Lambda and delivery to S3, Redshift, and OpenSearch, charging only for data volume with no idle costs during zero-traffic periods.
Use Kinesis Data Streams with on-demand capacity mode for auto-scaling ingestion, eliminating shard management and scaling to zero cost during idle periods with no provisioned capacity charges.
Use Lambda functions with event source mapping from Kinesis for transformation and enrichment, scaling from zero to thousands of concurrent executions automatically with per-invocation billing only.

explanation: Kinesis on-demand mode scales automatically from zero with no provisioned capacity, charging only for throughput used. Lambda with Kinesis event source mapping scales processing from zero concurrent executions with per-invocation pricing. Both are truly serverless with zero cost at zero traffic. MSK Serverless (C) still has minimum charges even with no traffic. Firehose (D) handles delivery but has limited transformation capabilities compared to Lambda and doesn't replace the ingestion layer.

stem: A company's application uses a single NAT Gateway for all internet-bound traffic from private subnets. The NAT Gateway processes 5 TB of data monthly at $0.045/GB, costing $225/month in data processing charges alone. Analysis shows that 80% of the traffic is to AWS services (S3, DynamoDB, SQS, ECR). Which optimization reduces NAT Gateway costs?

options.text: Create VPC gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB (free), and interface endpoints for SQS and ECR (per-hour + per-GB charges lower than NAT), routing AWS service traffic through endpoints instead of NAT Gateway.

Replace the single NAT Gateway with a NAT instance on a t3.micro for lower hourly costs, configure the NAT instance with enhanced networking for better throughput, and use Auto Scaling for high availability.
Add a second NAT Gateway in another AZ for load distribution, configure route tables to split traffic between both NAT Gateways, reducing per-gateway data processing and improving availability.
Migrate all private subnet workloads to public subnets with Elastic IPs, removing the need for NAT Gateway entirely, and use security groups to restrict inbound traffic from the internet.

explanation: S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints are free with no data processing charges. Interface endpoints for SQS and ECR charge less per GB than NAT Gateway. Routing 80% of traffic through endpoints reduces NAT Gateway data processing from 5 TB to 1 TB, saving approximately $180/month. NAT instance (B) has lower hourly cost but adds management overhead and reduced availability. Second NAT Gateway (C) doubles the hourly cost and doesn't reduce per-GB charges. Public subnets (D) expose workloads to the internet and violate security best practices.

stem: A company is modernizing its monolithic Spring Boot application by extracting microservices. The first service to extract handles user authentication and is called by all other modules. The monolith still handles remaining functionality. Both systems must work together during the transition. Which pattern enables the monolith and new microservice to coexist?

options.text: Replace the authentication module in the monolith with an HTTP client that calls the new authentication microservice, deploy both on the same ECS cluster sharing a service discovery namespace for communication.

Deploy the authentication microservice as a sidecar container alongside the monolith in the same ECS task definition, communicate via localhost, and gradually extract more services as additional sidecars.

Deploy the authentication microservice behind API Gateway, configure API Gateway to route /auth/* to the microservice and all other paths to the monolith's ALB, sharing the session store in ElastiCache Redis.

Keep the authentication module in the monolith unchanged, deploy the new microservice alongside it handling only new authentication requests, and use feature flags to gradually shift traffic from old to new.

explanation: API Gateway acts as the facade (Anti-Corruption Layer) routing authentication to the new microservice and everything else to the monolith. Shared session store in Redis ensures session continuity across both systems. This is the classic Strangler Fig implementation. Internal HTTP client (B) creates a hard dependency from monolith to microservice. Sidecar pattern (C) doesn't provide independent deployment and scaling. Feature flags without a routing layer (D) requires modifying the monolith's authentication logic.
